subject: Strategically closing voting sites

body:
Every suppressive action these vengeful partisans take shows their true colors. For all their talk about election integrity, voter ID, and not harming eligible voters, closing legitimate polling places to make it harder to vote only has one logical end result.
Attacks by opponents of voting rights on young voters, mail-in ballots, early voting, and more aren't about integrity and fairness. It's about protecting their own power at any cost and tilting the playing field before the game has even been played.
We must stand up to stop them at every turn. RUSH $35 or more today to help us fight back in North Carolina and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=032526_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NC Newsline: Amid protests, NC elections board rejects campus voting sites and Sunday voting in several counties [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=032526_3&amount=25]
We're now facing the repercussions of the partisan election takeover laws that went into effect at the end of 2024, Team.
To refresh your memory: After the 2024 elections and the defeat of a MAGA candidate for governor, opponents of voting rights in North Carolina jammed through a bill that took the power of the governor to appoint people to election boards and handed that to the state auditor . It's worth noting that the state auditor is the only statewide elected Republican, with Democrats winning the 2024 races for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, and secretary of state.
Now, among massive protests from young voters, the MAGA-fied North Carolina State Elections Board recently shot down proposals to continue having early voting sites on several universities around the state . These weren't new sites either; these were places where North Carolina had provided early voting locations for a decade or more.
This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. It's another demonstration of how opponents of voting rights in North Carolina are more focused on expanding and cementing their own power than they are in serving the people and having fair elections.
We have to fight these suppressive actions in North Carolina and any other state where opponents of voting rights try to replicate this. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today to help every eligible voter cast their ballot >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=032526_3&amount=35]

These new, highly partisan State Election Board members wouldn't even look the protestors in the eye or engage with their proposals. After the vote, Chairman Francis De Luca threatened to call the cops on students if they didn’t leave.
Need to better understand how this impacts young voters? Western Carolina University in Jackson County, for example, has had a polling place on campus since 2016 that’s been used in five general elections and four primaries, according to a document prepared for the board. The state board voted 3-2 to get rid of it.
Closing the campus voting site would not save money, but “ would create barriers to voting for young, rural residents ,” Jackson County Board member Betsy Swift told the state board. 64% of students don’t have vehicles to drive to the polling place, she said.
Without the on-campus site, the closest polling place for students will be a recreation center nearly two miles away. Students without transportation will have to walk along a four-lane highway and through a meadow to get there.
Voter suppression isn't just black and white photos of eligible voters being turned away from polling places. Voter suppression is making it harder for eligible voters to take part in our elections through onerous ID requirements, closing polling places, taking away voting locations, or ending mail-in voting. Every time someone makes it harder to cast your ballot, voters are suppressed.
It's not going to end until we stop them.
Opponents of voting rights aren't going to stop attacking our fundamental right to vote until we stop them at the ballot box and take away their power. Chip in $35 or whatever you can today to help fight back nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=032526_3&amount=35]

Did you see this? ^
**Donald Trump’s conservative-majority Supreme Court could limit mail-in voting and suppress your right to vote.**
Let me be extremely clear: **This is a blatant attempt by Donald Trump to skew elections in favor of Republicans ahead of this November where his extremist candidates and his dangerous agenda are on the ballot — including right here in New Mexico.**
Your right to vote is sacred, and for many, mail-in voting isn’t just convenient — it’s essential.
For rural and Tribal communities, active-duty military and overseas voters, seniors, people with disabilities, shift workers, students, caregivers, and anyone without reliable transportation or time off, vote-by-mail is often the only way to make their voices heard. Even Donald Trump himself uses vote-by-mail – but doesn't think you deserve that same right.
As New Mexico’s next governor, I will fight tooth and nail to defend your right to vote in free and fair elections, including your right to mail-in voting. **And if Trump doesn’t like that, he can sue me.**
**[_(Will you chip in $5 right now to help me win this November and protect your right to vote from GOP attacks?)_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5902?refcode=jtk500-fr-nd&amount=5&t=2&akid=8504%2E400544%2EP5EVk1)**

With voting rights, healthcare, affordability, and so much more at stake, we can’t give the GOP even an inch in this race. | | | Be fierce, Deb | | | | |

body:
AOC's newest bill
#
Any advancements in artificial intelligence _must_ benefit the working families of this country, while safeguarding our environment — and energy costs — for future generations.
That’s why Alexandria and Bernie Sanders introduced legislation today to **end construction on any new data centers until federal AI regulations are in place**.
These big tech companies are not paying for their own energy infrastructure. While the American people's energy bills are skyrocketing in order to pay for A.I. data centers, big tech continues to demand more.
More data centers, more energy, more data collection, more American jobs replaced by A.I. — all on the feet of the American people to pay.
But Alexandria came to Congress to legislate in a new way: **by really centering everyday people and the policies that benefit their lives**.
[Alexandria is 100% focused on fighting for us. She doesn’t do a single minute of fundraising ‘call-time’ asking wealthy people for big checks. subject: This will set the tone
body:
| | Peter – Bumping this email to the top of your inbox. Our FEC deadline is just days away, and we need to show unmistakable grassroots strength before our numbers go public.

In 2025 Minnesota got caught running what investigators called one of the largest welfare fraud schemes in American history. Billions in childcare subsidies gone, stolen by foreigners while American families couldn't find affordable care. Fake providers billing for children who never existed, while real money walked out the door because nobody was actually checking anything.
We have the exact same structural problem in Idaho.
Federal dollars flowing into a childcare subsidy program that's been running since the 1990s, with absolutely nobody able to criminally prosecute fraud against it. So on December 31st, Representative Josh Tanner and I sent [a letter to the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare](https://substack.com/redirect/4257c61b-bf06-45a1-8316-db2e88f0f58f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demanding they pause $14 million in new childcare appropriations until real fraud prevention got installed. I'd voted against Senate Bill 1206 during the 2025 session specifically because it dumped $14 million into new childcare subsidies with zero safeguards (e.g. money going out the door, kids unverified, fraud undetectable and unprosecutable).
We wanted enrollment verification, a review of past disbursements, inspection protocols, and a legislative briefing before another dollar moved. Pretty reasonable when you're watching Minnesota burn, right?
DHW took three months to respond. And it wasn't a fraud prevention plan.
It was a threat.
Because on March 9th, Director Juliet Charron [wrote to the Joint Finance-Appropriations Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/a86f4930-9be9-4061-a084-3821103c424e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) claiming ICCP had been operating without proper legal authority all along. No statutory basis, she said. Then the ultimatum: pass S1374 (a vendor-written expansion bill creating an AI fraud detection system and 600 new licensed childcare programs) or, she said, IDHW winds the whole thing down by end of fiscal year.
We asked them to stop the bleeding in December. And they handed us a bill to build 600 more places to bleed from, written by the contractor who'd profit from building them (just 3 months later).
What was actually in S1374? Provider-reported attendance verified by a fraud detection system that analyzes... provider-reported data. If providers are lying about attendance in the first place, analyzing their lies won't catch them. Real enrollment verification didn't make it in. Neither did spot checks or anything resembling actual inspection. Minnesota's fraud happened because providers self-reported attendance with nobody checking. S1374 just automates the same broken process.
So on March 12th, Senator Josh Keyser and I [went directly to Attorney General Raul Labrador](https://substack.com/redirect/45c517e5-c156-4420-9bb3-b071dc67dac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to ask basically: had the program actually been operating without legal authority for thirty years? And, do they have the legal authority to do this or not? Because Charron's argument, if true, changes everything.
The AG responded March 19th (last week):
_**
Chief Deputy Phil Skinner was clear: the program is legal.**_
Idaho Code 56-202 covers it because childcare assistance qualifies as both "public assistance" and "social services" under the statute's own definitions. Federal grant authority provides a second independent basis. And the legislature's repeated annual appropriation of ICCP funds constitutes ongoing affirmative endorsement of the program.
All that to say: IDHW's "we have no authority" argument didn't survive scrutiny.
The AG also noted the legislature could provide greater statutory clarity, putting the legal question fully to rest.
That's exactly what the bill we passed out of the Senate H&W committee today does ([SB 1419](https://substack.com/redirect/9822dd98-8032-468f-88d1-fe4310f8ad8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), among other things.
The program is legal. It's not going anywhere. It existed before any of us got here and it'll exist after we're all gone. And even though IDHW tried to use legal uncertainty as leverage, the AG disagreed, and now we're back to the question I was asking in December: _**who 's actually governing this thing?**_
Right now the answer is nobody. Not really.
Daycare providers have been billing the program for kids who never walked through the door. Real money going to fraudsters. And when that fraud gets caught? The Attorney General of Idaho cannot prosecute it criminally. At all (right now he has no authority to do anything about it except watch).
SB 1419 changes that. The AG gets _**concurrent prosecutorial authority**_ the moment it passes. Fraud becomes a criminal matter instead of a paperwork error that gets filed away.
And something that isn't anywhere in current law: providers who employ illegal aliens have been in this program the whole time (collecting from it). SB 1419 removes them permanently and says if you get caught with illegal labor, you're out for good.
Future expansion of the program requires the legislature to approve it in statute first (right now IDHW can grow it on administrative rules nobody voted on). So the hard sunset (i.e. expiration date) in 2028 means it doesn't roll forward on autopilot. And it'll be the legislature, not some agency, who has to actively decide to keep it going.
None of that was in the vendor bill IDHW originally gave us. That one gave us an AI system and 600 new licensed facilities with no meaningful verification that any child being billed for actually exists. Bureaucratic theater dressed up as accountability.
But the bill we passed out of committee today is the actual enforcement.
A yes vote today didn't create or fund a "new government daycare program." It does neither. The ICCP has been running thirty years and funding decisions are in entirely separate appropriation bills we still have coming up (and I'll be a no on those BTW).
Bottom-line is: if we voted no on SB 1419 today, it'd mean the fraud doesn't stop.
_**The program would just keep running the same broken way, the AG would keep watching with nothing he can legally do about it, and we 'd be waiting for the next Minnesota to happen here instead.**_
IDHW tried to use a legal threat to force through their vendor bill. The AG said no. So the legislature got to do what it should've done years ago: put real teeth in a program that's been running on the honor system since 1990.
That's SB 1419.
That's why I voted yes today.
Because nobody wants Idaho to become Minnesota.

clean_body: I asked for fraud enforcement in December 2025. Here's where we're at today. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more I asked for fraud enforcement in December 2025. Here's where we're at today. | | | Mar 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | In 2025 Minnesota got caught running what investigators called one of the largest welfare fraud schemes in American history. Billions in childcare subsidies gone, stolen by foreigners while American families couldn't find affordable care. Fake providers billing for children who never existed, while real money walked out the door because nobody was actually checking anything. We have the exact same structural problem in Idaho. Federal dollars flowing into a childcare subsidy program that's been running since the 1990s, with absolutely nobody able to criminally prosecute fraud against it. So on December 31st, Representative Josh Tanner and I sent demanding they pause $14 million in new childcare appropriations until real fraud prevention got installed. I'd voted against Senate Bill 1206 during the 2025 session specifically because it dumped $14 million into new childcare subsidies with zero safeguards (e.g. money going out the door, kids unverified, fraud undetectable and unprosecutable). We wanted enrollment verification, a review of past disbursements, inspection protocols, and a legislative briefing before another dollar moved. Pretty reasonable when you're watching Minnesota burn, right? DHW took three months to respond. And it wasn't a fraud prevention plan. It was a threat. Because on March 9th, Director Juliet Charron claiming ICCP had been operating without proper legal authority all along. No statutory basis, she said. Then the ultimatum: pass S1374 (a vendor-written expansion bill creating an AI fraud detection system and 600 new licensed childcare programs) or, she said, IDHW winds the whole thing down by end of fiscal year. We asked them to stop the bleeding in December. And they handed us a bill to build 600 more places to bleed from, written by the contractor who'd profit from building them (just 3 months later). What was actually in S1374? Provider-reported attendance verified by a fraud detection system that analyzes... provider-reported data. If providers are lying about attendance in the first place, analyzing their lies won't catch them. Real enrollment verification didn't make it in. Neither did spot checks or anything resembling actual inspection. Minnesota's fraud happened because providers self-reported attendance with nobody checking. S1374 just automates the same broken process. So on March 12th, Senator Josh Keyser and I to ask basically: had the program actually been operating without legal authority for thirty years? And, do they have the legal authority to do this or not? Because Charron's argument, if true, changes everything. The AG responded March 19th (last week): Chief Deputy Phil Skinner was clear: the program is legal. Idaho Code 56-202 covers it because childcare assistance qualifies as both "public assistance" and "social services" under the statute's own definitions. Federal grant authority provides a second independent basis. And the legislature's repeated annual appropriation of ICCP funds constitutes ongoing affirmative endorsement of the program. All that to say: IDHW's "we have no authority" argument didn't survive scrutiny. The AG also noted the legislature could provide greater statutory clarity, putting the legal question fully to rest. That's exactly what the bill we passed out of the Senate H&W committee today does (), among other things. The program is legal. It's not going anywhere. It existed before any of us got here and it'll exist after we're all gone. And even though IDHW tried to use legal uncertainty as leverage, the AG disagreed, and now we're back to the question I was asking in December: who 's actually governing this thing? Right now the answer is nobody. Not really. Daycare providers have been billing the program for kids who never walked through the door. Real money going to fraudsters. And when that fraud gets caught? The Attorney General of Idaho cannot prosecute it criminally. At all (right now he has no authority to do anything about it except watch). SB 1419 changes that. The AG gets concurrent prosecutorial authority the moment it passes. Fraud becomes a criminal matter instead of a paperwork error that gets filed away. And something that isn't anywhere in current law: providers who employ illegal aliens have been in this program the whole time (collecting from it). SB 1419 removes them permanently and says if you get caught with illegal labor, you're out for good. Future expansion of the program requires the legislature to approve it in statute first (right now IDHW can grow it on administrative rules nobody voted on). So the hard sunset (i.e. expiration date) in 2028 means it doesn't roll forward on autopilot. And it'll be the legislature, not some agency, who has to actively decide to keep it going. None of that was in the vendor bill IDHW originally gave us. That one gave us an AI system and 600 new licensed facilities with no meaningful verification that any child being billed for actually exists. Bureaucratic theater dressed up as accountability. But the bill we passed out of committee today is the actual enforcement. A yes vote today didn't create or fund a "new government daycare program." It does neither. The ICCP has been running thirty years and funding decisions are in entirely separate appropriation bills we still have coming up (and I'll be a no on those BTW). Bottom-line is: if we voted no on SB 1419 today, it'd mean the fraud doesn't stop. The program would just keep running the same broken way, the AG would keep watching with nothing he can legally do about it, and we 'd be waiting for the next Minnesota to happen here instead. IDHW tried to use a legal threat to force through their vendor bill. The AG said no. So the legislature got to do what it should've done years ago: put real teeth in a program that's been running on the honor system since 1990. That's SB 1419. That's why I voted yes today. Because nobody wants Idaho to become Minnesota. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Brian Lenney ? ?

## Jury Rules Social Media Liable for Teen's Addiction
A Los Angeles jury ruled Wednesday that Meta and YouTube must pay a combined $6 million in damages to a 20-year-old woman who said [the platforms hooked her as a child](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO4zAMBdDT2J0DmZIlu1CxTbpsu6VBk0zChWwFspAgtx84A8wFpiQJEP_9f5f5gpp0u_3FVWK95nmT156kVinznkkxrcKKyKxUNW9PKawzGPCdsR34mVHTe3Ytx6sIiG0l9iG4oZ-CH9t7tDT6ZZz6iYwlDHYxzsskyERiEcZW4_HNWPC9MRP402B7Rj-iY7HLtIyNM8Jaczn9z7rVu1zTOz-lnCivbYr3Wh97Y_80cG7gjI8DcJyOoVSlJA2cvyndx9L9YLpajm3CbpDBmTAYsDzaQMQUPDnCoQeZYOC2RH68NCXdfWicua2o6ROg_qq1Z4SvAAAA__-UPn_a) through design features like infinite scroll, autoplay, and algorithmically timed notifications. The plaintiff, known as K.G.M., testified she began using YouTube at 6 and Instagram at 9, eventually spending [16 hours in a single day](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdI7MGmwoXPwNXf72SrSJl7A5Y0fYBPH2J3KPcN1II32a-b6u4xU5cHz8x4VcmdIYac-BSqF1zOnOGBbyjOg93wun-KbV8wgKjFRaghk9cjjGpvJuIgLSFbna2qate2u6anZatVY3rUXSmiaynbVTj1AbY5quN3XF7qQpDaZWqgdzaXXt0XTYeNK3_taJRpHnktbLM3EsM03hSG9aL_e0VMHNpbyy0P8EDAKGeLxSLmclYDjBAgalz9wKGLYsz38Chue2HrLgN2WZouSYCz5WXCRGL4-0le1GkqP8VSA_DmSe0-7THgUM1er8a-cQOBsrGvVYkMNnUPmTxbeDnwAAAP__ZziFWg) on Instagram, spiraling into depression, anxiety, and body dysmorphia. Jurors targeted platform design itself as a defective product, a legal theory one tech policy professor compared to the tobacco lawsuits. More than [1,500 similar suits](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL8GOpCxjR0XLq6hy7VXosW7hI0MjowTxN-fuF-4bqSRZvTez328A0feHt-wki9zGjc69kilUB73FBjiSsgAiBwKp-1DGXmUQppGqEaaEYHjOeoa_UwkSdXkO2t13zlrbvXiSc2qo6l3NBllMShlaHKWEJ3tg9U1-2tNKGk6IZw0ba86BHMDjaQmN90qLQi5pNw-E29loTme6UO5DWmto19Kee2V-qrkUMnhOI72hCWlq63kcOFUcoBcOES6YoDIc8obQ_N857OZecO9WalAc6Z3eU_UdFb30plet0tZY509vg6OkXdjKy0eK3D8Oy__Mvbx8jcAAP__oTCApw) against Meta, YouTube, Snapchat, and TikTok are pending in California courts alone.
## Iran Rejects Ceasefire, Issues Counterproposal
Iran on Wednesday [rejected Trump's ceasefire proposal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJy8kbGu4yAQRb8Gd0Qw2GAXFNu4y7ZbWhMzxLPCYGE2Uf5-5fcLT3r1vbpHV-fPfbkjJ87P37iTb7Esmd5notaoLmdZGdNOgRFD4LVxyS-qgRdQYKUyEuwSkNNn6bvgIxGQ6chr5_pBT86O3eaddRhidCP2YGBQpBSNNDxw0kZNeu3YX2vKgNVKTWBvg9EB7Yh9IPOYHqPoFQVupd7-Fs5to5g-5UX1tpa9S35r7TiF-SVgFjC3jTZO6coEzEdJvH4EzJwb1YzXA0wC5mFUSrtJcsUsS4xUT7mWf1frqOUoJyb5xiopBwHzDyC66sPx5pT4tE706rkjfyG69i0tLw__AwAA___6G6Mz) and issued a five-point counterproposal demanding war reparations, guarantees against future attacks, and full sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign minister told state media the country doesn't want a ceasefire, saying it'll end the war on its own terms. The White House insisted talks remain "productive," even as the U.S. [deployed 82nd Airborne paratroopers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdEb2AgYKF2noLm1KtLDL3UYGn2zn0P19RH4h3Ugjzei9r9t8Qwly3D9xZ1-2OB985sClcJpzXAXDziSIRLIWiceLE8kMBpw2jQY3E0p4z21FfmMGbir2tu_bzo69G6qHd2zcsJgWqbUbdASjHbAbezt2g122tRJ_rZkGnDVmBFd3jSV0A7bEzTIug2oNk5SY6u8oR3nwFt7xxale414F_yjlmVXzoWBSMJ3nWa9LviiuXsF0RQXTj86a-BniWw9wkEZJS0wHa0l46F2IAmvGXBRMVfL0PCUEya5XrbnvKOHvrvzL0cvDbwAAAP__4517Dw) to supplement roughly 50,000 troops already in the region. An Iranian drone attack Wednesday [ignited a fuel tank](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2yozAQBODTiEyUfkBAoGATsvfSDalBGsHskyWXGNvl2295r7BZR91d3--v7QsoUzm-4YaeU90Kvq6MzNi2qwaCfMNIADFSYKrliS3SZpRxUllp3BaB8nsbuugTokHbodfTNIx6mdzcnT4FCPuidrvoWSs1RodBh3GyapwtauzIf9qUNU4rtRjXj1ZHcDMMEe2-7LMYFEbi2vo_lQqfmPK7PrH1od667E_m-yXsL2FWYVYsR6br7CFDg53e0BdkYdZvfF3CrMcjJ2HWz6Iwq7KfPAqzJmoogeXP4wXEEqjda2MJibHJ2GrBS57EMj0wS4byI-FJ8AGRcGAJ7675eH9RznS5SQzquAHlfw_5v1if3vwNAAD__6RSjHE) at Kuwait International Airport, while Israel continued striking targets in Tehran.
## Baseball Season Opens Today
The 2026 MLB season officially opens today with 11 games across the country, following Wednesday night's streaming opener on Netflix between the Yankees and the Giants. [See today's schedule here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCnMV2QvSYGChd_Q5e_vdJas0vYk8ER9gXl7U856Z7gupFG-kaaj1u4oSTZ7_9xY1-XHHY-S-Ja-Qglz4JpYxJEIpmr5P3JB0kADe6i7QVcIJT0Cl1DfmEGtg170_fd1Yy9G5rVR4hsjR0HB-Riz5rGDtmYAZYRZ20b8W9NW3BG6xFce7WG0A3YEds4xkF1mklqPtrPLHtdeUmv_OSjnfPWJL_W-ijK_lMwKZjO82y5PPZ3qWDaUlQwlXll-kqsYAoKJsL6jr-zzeHpcUpKUlyvOn3fUNIPXv_0yNPDdwAAAP__16tyuA). All eyes are on the Los Angeles Dodgers, who enter the season as back-to-back World Series champions with a league-leading $398 million payroll. Tickets to tonight's home opener in LA are [averaging $392 on the resale market](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQAL_GdEZmDQYKF2noLm1KtLALt4nByLaO3N8_3fuFV480I82fx_xACXLuv_FgX7Y4n3znwKVwmnNcBcPBJIhEshaJ54sTyQwGnDZWg5sJJbzntiK_MQPbin3T923XjL0bqqcnssswgKNtQNN1Iy9mhG400FjYmLES_7EZC64xZgRXd7YhdAO2xHYZl0G1hklKTPXfKGd58hbe8cWpXuNRBf8s5crK_lIwKZju-663-D_ghyqY8hVTyQqmgJoi7Zyyjhefcu6a8K2LrP-46CvJyrlKnq5bQpDsetWa_UAJ35nyozcvD18BAAD__-RCeaw), making it the most expensive Opening Day game in MLB history. This season brings the sport's biggest rule change in years: the [automated ball-strike challenge system](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO5CAQRU-DM1q4bGMIHGxCNptuaGFT7q7dAixg2vLtVzNXmPhLX--9Px_rhyem9PztIy7tyGvCqzK2hmWteSfPEQN5HwLtjXJ6Ywm0ggIt1SBBr8ET3-vYheVABBw6XPp5Hqfeztp0r0XtvbKbRrub2ZrpsEHjsetpnsbjsKPtaPl6UwPoXikL-jENffDa-DHgsNnNiFFhoJbL42-m1F548J3fWB57jh0vr9bOKoZfApwAd13XA-uZvkYBLvImwNWWyy3ArQIcBQFuNGAMzEaAyycmSk8Z_C2_tSJvsqKvOcmz4Jvwkv6z5egbBrl5ZllboX8o95dnxvREWe_aMMryydiVJZwXMVPVsxjVM3rib9L2o7zvBf4HAAD__9YvjzM). Players can now challenge an umpire's ball-or-strike call by tapping their helmet, triggering an instant review using Hawk-Eye camera technology. I wanted to take a moment to introduce myself, Fellow Patriot.

My name is Kurt Alme, and I am running for U.S. Senate because I believe Montana deserves leadership rooted in service, accountability, and in the conservative values we were raised on.

I am a Montana native. I was born in Great Falls to two public school teachers who taught me from an early age that hard work, education, and giving back _**matter**_.

Growing up, I lived all across the state - Dillon, Victor, Helena, and Miles City - giving me a deep appreciation for our communities and the people who make Montana great.

[](http://links.kurtalme.com/u/click?_t=13f02befef694c2ea0e5bfe0ba1ceb44&_m=d759c18e55d8430e872da4facbaec119&_e=QE3Js41gd-G6xWr_h4a4QWJxwAsM1_h33n_zEe1X_bCV6jBCMDemHmNSj_LB_u6dzzhFDsWi80giMPJ5_ciCG_aMvTs6kM8TTAgYCbr-XOJH6NRRrONJJRk8wistC4E_PRDuhT2c3VPcqezsFKWFiGD9CpmsTVJaPo7Q4hENQSiqLnWSCqf34Lx7plPN4IMmiKPss-IBUUvCY42xYov0bf7POc3Ohf0eds8pJILIQ1HKqAkUe8Fc1f9pg6EnrRraIZpA3wAJ891kUB2GqMNPHOoIjWZcSUflvNpVIWU4iP5OKXJBHRqLlkwOyA3IIw2Vf9L3oGVYuDsXhkBAV3_NVF8e1InMkMrNcSPC2LbsjOvxXwTpC1v6NJ6_MsWCBLtq1f4Se2wdVsgSU0ZfO9RChdXhKuIojxmlnF92cXYhNeSB4WwHpg0gGIgiQqx5U5-LS2JrJt7ZobQ-V6Tz8XrfJiGTBE_uX3_-LcSiLlWHHQrt8Kut_WQjeOgNKWF32JettLOnYzHxAmvBROONjF6yHzLzYPz8j7CjoCD9GOB_q299kPq0vH59m7JT9uf90bCD4Pir64LdzX9TiPRhAej42yezWnONLzK6r-Pnbitwmf5ZvYi2p6FVy7gATcpn6G4-BFJYYMwqebh8wCFX8i7CzCnQ_JWUTEN25lcFWaQlstTrt-1JO7RCuTZ6DT-aMpqr)
I earned a business degree at the University of Colorado and a law degree at Harvard. But I always knew I would come home. _**And I did.**_

I came back to Montana to serve. First as a prosecutor, and then as Montana's U.S. Attorney, I fought fraud, violent crime and drug trafficking. As a Budget Director for Montana, I worked to balance the budget, cut taxes and keep government accountable. I've also helped lead many nonprofit organizations focused on caring for our youth, seniors, sick and mentally ill to strengthen our communities and serve Montana families. I've dedicated my life to service, and I am ready to keep serving our country.

I've spent my career getting the job done - not chasing headlines.

Now, I am running for U.S. Senate because I've seen firsthand the pressure Montana families are feeling - and Washington isn't working the way it should.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Monetary systems come and go.

Excessive debt, inflationary pressures, and geopolitical shifts drive these resets.

It happened to the Classical Gold Standard. Currencies were fully backed by gold. Then massive debt financing for WWI broke the system.

It happened to the Bretton Woods System after WWII. Where the U.S. dollar was pegged to gold and other currencies pegged to the dollar.

Now... it's happening to the current Jamaica Accords System that President Nixon put us on.

Who will benefit as the current system gets replaced?

Anyone holding gold. Because gold is the only true form of money. Central banks, sovereign nations, and major institutional investors are stockpiling as much as they can.

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. name: Barack Obama
subject: How Democrats respond matters
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President
body:
This is about preserving our democracy not just for November, but for decades to come.

---
Peter, here’s something I believe in strongly: Politicians shouldn’t get to draw their own district lines and hand-pick their own voters. **Citizens should get to decide who represents them. ** That’s how democracy is supposed to work. And it’s why Eric Holder and I teamed up to build the National Democratic Redistricting Committee with a mission of fighting for fair maps. The truth is not everyone wants to play by the rules. In the last year, we’ve witnessed Republican-controlled states take the unprecedented step of redrawing their congressional maps in the middle of the decade. They even admitted they’re doing this to gain an unfair advantage in the midterm elections. As Democrats, we can’t just copy the same bad behavior. Nobody wants to see us abandon the rule of law or show zero regard for the truth. If that’s how Democrats fight back, then we lose what we’re fighting for in the first place. **But that doesn’t mean we have to sit on our hands, either.** We can’t pretend this redistricting crisis isn’t happening. That’s why states like California and Virginia have decided to fight back in a way that lets the people decide — putting referendums on the ballot that would temporarily level the playing field by ensuring Republicans can’t gerrymander their way to a House majority in the midterms. California voters overwhelmingly approved that approach last fall. Next month, Virginians have the opportunity to do the same. Right now, volunteers are actively organizing to help get out the vote in this special election — in the first weekend of early voting, our team reached over 350,000 Virginians. Make no mistake: Republicans are desperate to hold onto power and avoid accountability. But this movement was built to stop them. We might not be able to outspend the powerful interests on the other side, but we can out-organize them, out-work them, and outlast them. **Each of us has a role to play to help preserve our democracy — not just in November, but for decades to come.[Will you make a donation to the NDRC today and invest in this critical pro-democracy work?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128069754/610172961/-1096702678?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_MarchObamaNOR_email_20260326-NDRC-Tier1-MarchObamaNOR_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260326-NDRC-Tier1-MarchObamaNOR_&utm_campaign=MarchObamaNOR&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjNjNWMzYTUxLTBiMjktZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=x0c3vXsOilNDmIIY6VZDgrwfMneTWyDZC3HSmTjVFGk=)** Let’s go, Barack Obama | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128069755/610172976/-1096702678?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_MarchObamaNOR_email_20260326-NDRC-Tier1-MarchObamaNOR_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260326-NDRC-Tier1-MarchObamaNOR_&utm_campaign=MarchObamaNOR&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjNjNWMzYTUxLTBiMjktZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=x0c3vXsOilNDmIIY6VZDgrwfMneTWyDZC3HSmTjVFGk=)

Do you know how much Jeff Bezos would have to find in his pocket for it to mean the same thing to him? **$6 million.** Yeah, that's right: Five bucks to you is, like, $6 million to billionaire Jeff Bezos. That is how rich that guy is. And it's not just Bezos. Today, the top one-tenth of one percent owe nearly as much wealth as the bottom 90% of all families combined. Enough is enough. It is time to unrig the economy. And that starts with the ultra-wealthy, paying their fair share. **I've just reintroduced my Ultra-Millionaire Tax plan to make billionaires finally pay their fair share in taxes. I want to share more below on what this plan calls for and how much it would generate if we just tax billionaires two cents on every dollar of their net worth above $50 million —[**but we need to show that this plan has massive, public support. Will you add your name to show your support for our two-cent wealth tax?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-wealth-tax/?source=EMZ30J_TAX_E_20260326_V1S1&refcode=EMZ30J_TAX_E_20260326_V1S1&t=8&akid=2831%2E4032634%2EeHnM9Q)** | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-wealth-tax/?source=EMZ30J_TAX_E_20260326_V1S1&refcode=EMZ30J_TAX_E_20260326_V1S1&t=9&akid=2831%2E4032634%2EeHnM9Q)
---
Over the past few decades, the rich have gotten richer while working families have struggled just to get by.
When we first introduced the Ultra-Millionaire Tax, economists projected it would raise $3 trillion over a decade. That estimate has now doubled to $6 trillion.
Not because the tax changed — because billionaire wealth exploded.
While working families were figuring out how to pay their bills, billionaires were doubling their fortunes.
So what do they do with all that money, besides buying yachts, mansions, and sending Katy Perry into space?
Well, they hire lobbyists to protect their tax breaks, then push to cut the very programs that keep working families afloat.
**They rig the game, and then they rig it again.**
If just one billionaire like Jeff Bezos paid under this plan, we could fund insulin for everyone in America who needs it — and still have money left over.
Now imagine what’s possible if every ultra-millionaire and billionaire chipped in just a few cents on the dollar.
The Ultra-Millionaire Tax asks the wealthiest 0.15% of households to pay 2% on wealth over $50 million — and it closes the loopholes that let them avoid paying in the first place. That means:
* **Rebuild and strengthen the IRS** so it has the staff, technology, and resources to enforce the Ultra-Millionaire Tax.
* **Stronger audits** ensure the ultra-wealthy actually pay what they owe.
* **An exit tax** that requires anyone with over $50 million in wealth who renounces U.S. citizenship to pay 40% on wealth above $50 million.
* **Better asset valuation tools** to give the IRS the power to accurately assess private businesses, artwork, and other hard-to-value property.
* **More transparency and accountability,** with banks and third parties reporting to the IRS, and penalties for anyone who hides or underreports wealth.

**With my two-cent wealth tax, we could make the American Dream a reality.**
We could expand child care, lower housing costs, cut child poverty, strengthen Medicare, provide paid family leave, and make college more affordable — all by simply asking the ultra-wealthy to finally pay their fair share.
It's time for a wealth attack in America. Let's get this done.
[**Add your name today and stand with me for a tax code that works for everyone, not just the ultra-wealthy.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-wealth-tax/?source=EMZ30J_TAX_E_20260326_V1S1&refcode=EMZ30J_TAX_E_20260326_V1S1&t=10&akid=2831%2E4032634%2EeHnM9Q)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

clean_body: | | | | Peter, Imagine this: A man steps outside his own home in a quiet neighborhood. Suddenly, violence erupts, his kneecap shattered in a brutal attack. His car torched. His family terrorized for years, children taunted with slurs in the streets, living under police protection for nearly a decade. This isn't a scene from some distant war zone. This happened in Bradford, England – to Nissar Hussain. His only "crime"? Leaving Islam and embracing Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. For 17 years, Nissar endured relentless persecution from his former community. The Church of England? SILENT. Not one bishop stood with him or his family. But Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member, refused to stand by. We brought Nissar here to the U.S. to help him share his story, and he is now fighting back boldly – in part by pursuing a groundbreaking legal case against 11 countries that still mandate death for apostasy. Nissar's story is heartbreaking, but it's not isolated. Over 380 million Christians face severe persecution globally, and the numbers are growing. In Iran, 254 believers were arrested in 2025 alone for simply practicing their faith, escalating further amid the regime's war on Christians. In Nigeria, thousands have been slaughtered by Islamist militants: entire villages massacred, girls held captive for years, all because they refused to deny Christ. In Pakistan, blasphemy laws are twisted to destroy Christian lives. In North Korea, owning a Bible can mean a lifetime in a labor camp. It is for all of these reasons that Save the Persecuted Christians is relentlessly educating Americans and rallying the faithful to recognize the threat before it takes deeper root here. A powerful example: Our ongoing education and advocacy efforts helped fuel the overwhelming success on March 3, when 95% of Texas Republican primary voters stood up and voted to ban Sharia law – sending a clear, faithful message: We will not let this ideology gain a foothold in America and threaten our freedoms or our persecuted brothers and sisters in Christ. The threat is real. Persecution that starts overseas doesn't always stay there. We must be extra vigilant, and we need your help right now to keep pushing back. Your gift, especially a monthly commitment through The Defenders Guild, multiplies our impact and sustains the fight against this growing evil. Paul wrote in Galatians 6:2, “Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” That is our mandate as the Body of Christ. The Church must rise in one spirit, refusing silence in the face of darkness. Thank you for your faithfulness and courage in this hour. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The decision by the Connecticut Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) to approve the sale of Aquarion Water Company to the South Central Connecticut Regional Water Authority (RWA) raises serious concerns about cost, accountability, and long-term impact on Connecticut ratepayers.
This isn't abstract--it's about affordability and public trust.
Ryan Fazio and many other Republicans in Hartford have been raising alarms about transactions like this for years, warning that they can shift financial burden onto residents while reducing transparency around long-term cost control.
What makes this even more notable is the response from William Tong. In his statement following the approval, he made clear that PURA did not meaningfully account for the widespread public opposition to this deal.
As AG Tong said "_This is a $6 billion gift to Eversource, to be paid by Connecticut families and towns over the next 40 years. Literally no one wanted this deal except for the utility executives looking to cash out._ "
That matters.
Because when broad, bipartisan, and local opposition--from residents to municipal leaders--is raised and then effectively dismissed, it sends a message: public input is secondary.
And this is not an isolated example.
Connecticut has seen extensive public testimony and submissions across multiple issues--medical freedom, the restoration of religious exemptions, and parental rights in areas like homeschooling--where large segments of the public have shown up, spoken clearly, and engaged in the process.
Yet too often, those voices are acknowledged procedurally and then disregarded substantively.
That pattern raises a larger concern: whether public participation is being treated as a formality rather than a meaningful input into decision-making.
It is also important to remember that this very transaction was previously rejected by PURA in November when Eversource Energy sought to sell Aquarion. That earlier decision underscores just how significant the reversal is--and raises real questions about what changed between then and now. The short answer is nothing changed - just the wrong result for Connecticut.
_At a time when Connecticut residents are already burdened by rising utility costs and broader concerns about government responsiveness, decisions like this should reflect caution, transparency, and respect for public input --not a pattern of dismissal._
Hartford isn't listening.
And Connecticut residents are paying the price.
Everyone says they stand for affordability.
**But when the decisions are made, only one side is held accountable for the damage --and Connecticut residents are left paying for it.**

It's disgraceful that Trump wants to limit Americans' right to vote when he personally just voted by mail in Florida's most recent election.

Friend,

Five years ago, I gathered with patriots from all corners of America to protest the certification of the 2020 election results.

All we wanted was for President Trump to get a fair shake, for mail-in vote counts to be redone, and to ensure no fraud had taken place. However, President Trump's enemies saw us coming, and they were ready and waiting to pull off perhaps the biggest psy-op America has ever seen.

Capitol Police officers welcomed many J6ers into the building, with some even providing off-the-cuff tours as they ushered protestors through the halls of the Capitol.

All of a sudden, though, things took a very dark turn...
* A Capitol Police officer murdered Ashli Babbitt.
* Overzealous officers assaulted protestors.
* Rosann Boyland was trampled to death in the panic that ensued as the Capitol Police swiftly turned on peaceful protestors.

For many, like myself, this day marked the beginning of a years-long political persecution that tore families apart, devastated finances, and even denied many of us our freedom and our fundamental human rights.

It also motivated me to start Stand in the Gap -- a commitment to stand in solidarity with and fight for those who are being overlooked or mistreated.

Our goal is to provide support and advocacy for those in need, ensuring they aren't left to face their challenges alone.

These J6ers are our neighbors. They are sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, mothers and fathers. It is up to us to ensure that they have the resources needed to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity.

We were founded to "stand in the gap" for those in prison and those navigating life after incarceration.

clean_body: If you are willing to stand with me to help these patriots rebuild their lives, please join me today by donating whatever you can generously afford to help Stand in the Gap today. Friend, Five years ago, I gathered with patriots from all corners of America to protest the certification of the 2020 election results. All we wanted was for President Trump to get a fair shake, for mail-in vote counts to be redone, and to ensure no fraud had taken place. However, President Trump's enemies saw us coming, and they were ready and waiting to pull off perhaps the biggest psy-op America has ever seen. Capitol Police officers welcomed many J6ers into the building, with some even providing off-the-cuff tours as they ushered protestors through the halls of the Capitol. All of a sudden, though, things took a very dark turn... A Capitol Police officer murdered Ashli Babbitt. Overzealous officers assaulted protestors. Rosann Boyland was trampled to death in the panic that ensued as the Capitol Police swiftly turned on peaceful protestors. For many, like myself, this day marked the beginning of a years-long political persecution that tore families apart, devastated finances, and even denied many of us our freedom and our fundamental human rights. It also motivated me to start Stand in the Gap -- a commitment to stand in solidarity with and fight for those who are being overlooked or mistreated. Our goal is to provide support and advocacy for those in need, ensuring they aren't left to face their challenges alone. Stand in the Gap originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping the recently released J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. Surprisingly, there are very few resources for people who are released from prison, particularly if they are conservative, America First activists, or who supported President Trump. These J6ers are our neighbors. They are sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, mothers and fathers. It is up to us to ensure that they have the resources needed to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. We were founded to "stand in the gap" for those in prison and those navigating life after incarceration. Our mission is to ensure that every J6er receives the help they need to heal - physically, mentally, emotionally, spiritually, and financially - to reintegrate into society. But they need your help to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. Sincerely, Shane Jenkins Founder and Executive Director of Stand in the Gap P.S. Like all of my interviews, these conversations are meant to be a place where you’ll hear fair, honest, and direct thinking from people who truly know the subject, without talking points or ideological spin. My goal is to offer context and clarity you do not often find elsewhere, with grounded insight that helps explain what is actually happening in the world and why it matters. As Easter and Passover approach, I am reminded that faith can bring comfort, perspective, and hope when the world feels unsettled. To all who will be celebrating, I wish you and your family peace, renewal, and many blessings in the days ahead. -John | | | | | While I don't enjoy asking for donations, it's a necessary part of our effort to fight for a better America. This kind of attention is powerful: but it also means our message is being amplified, and opponents are looking for ways to silence conservative voices. We need to turn this moment into momentum so we can keep pushing for real solutions: lower property taxes, accountability in Concord, secure borders, and protections for the Second Amendment and parental control over education. #
Peter —
There is something happening in Texas.
A new kind of politics is being born right here.
The number of young people who voted in the primary is unprecedented.
The number of first-time voters who voted in the primary is unprecedented.
The number of Independents and Republicans who voted in the Democratic primary is unprecedented.
The people of Texas have given this country a little bit of hope. And a little bit of hope is a dangerous thing.
It doesn’t matter what happens in the Republican runoff. We already know who we’re running against: the billionaire megadonors and their corrupt political system.
We are running against this broken system and the powerful people who broke it.
They’re scared of the movement we’re building together. So they’re going to throw everything they have at us.
They’ll call me a radical leftist and a fake Christian. They’ll call our movement un-Texan, un-American. They’ll call us a threat.
The only truth is: we are a threat — a threat to their corrupt system.
The status quo is fighting back, and it will be well-funded. Those at the top can raise and spend limitless sums of billionaire and corporate cash to keep the system rigged.

disclaimer_text: paid for by Joe Jaworski Campaign
body:
The right to vote is the foundation of everything. If that right is weakened, everything else follows. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jaworskifortexas.com/last-night-14193620?e=5d8d80652b)

| | , **The right to vote is the foundation of everything in our country.** If that right is weakened, everything else follows. Right now in Texas, we are seeing the opposite of what democracy demands. Laws that make it harder to register. Harder to vote. Harder to participate. That is not how the system is supposed to work. As your Attorney General, I will create a **Division of Elections and Voter Encouragement** with a goal to expand participation and make voting easier for every eligible Texan. First, we will enforce the law that is already on the books. Texas Election Code section 13.046(d) requires that high school seniors be offered the opportunity to register to vote. I will make sure that happens. **Every year. In every school. No exceptions.** Second, we will challenge unconstitutional voter suppression laws wherever they appear. If a law violates the Constitution, we will take it to court and we will fight to overturn it. Third, we will use the full power of the Attorney General’s office to encourage participation. That means clear information, access, and a visible commitment to making sure Texans can exercise their rights. Young Texans should leave high school ready to vote. College students should feel empowered to participate. Working Texans should not face unnecessary barriers just to have their voice heard. The Attorney General should be a champion for voters. That is exactly what I will be. [**Will you help me empower our people to vote? Please contribute today and help me win this election. The stakes are high and we are ready.**](https://jaworskifortexas.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e1f50319ad85f5f9e5c11ac9&id=28d8af89b7&e=5d8d80652b) Onward,

...and hitting the road!
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260326-1-b&t=1&akid=11340%2E3935704%2Eru-7mT)

Gabby Giffords here, and I wanted to share something exciting with you.
I’m hitting the road to help rally for gun safety candidates across the country and win back a majority in Congress. Our ability to take real action on public safety — and save lives from gun violence — could be decided by just a few hundred votes in November, so we’re not taking anything for granted.
I’m fired up to win. If you’re like me, I hope you’ll consider donating to GIFFORDS before our first end-of-quarter deadline of the year:
**[https://go.giffords.org/go/EOQ](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260326-1-b&t=2&akid=11340%2E3935704%2Eru-7mT)**
As I travel the country, the one thing I hear over and over is that Americans are tired of thoughts and prayers. They are fed up with politicians who refuse to act while our loved ones are killed because of guns.
I agree.
We cannot afford to play it safe anymore. That’s why GIFFORDS is going on offense for the midterm elections.
We have already endorsed dozens of candidates who have the courage to take on the gun lobby — and many will come down to the wire in their races. I’ll be traveling these next few months to get our message in front of persuadable voters.
But that takes a lot of resources, which is why I need to ask for your help.
**[Can you please make a contribution to GIFFORDS before our March 31st fundraising deadline? Your donations will help us overcome the massive spending from the gun lobby and mobilize — and it adds up quickly when everyone is chipping in.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260326-1-b&t=3&akid=11340%2E3935704%2Eru-7mT)

Actress Sydney Sweeney **[sent her love to US troops serving overseas, including her younger brother Trent,](https://substack.com/redirect/c01096ec-6134-4eb4-b3de-f6912e68a5b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** an Air Force staff sergeant deployed abroad, posting Wednesday "receiving calls from my bro always make me happy when he's deployed" alongside a screenshot of their video call. # **Melania Trump meets new American-made AI robot! What happens next is amazing...**
A humanoid robot walked the White House red carpet **[alongside First Lady Melania Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/ee5480dd-b944-4763-9c4b-dbf76dda60a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Wednesday for the final day of her Fostering the Future Together global initiative summit focused on empowering children through education, innovation, technology, and AI.
Figure 03, introduced in October 2025 by California-based startup Figure AI as a third-generation robot designed to help with household tasks like laundry, cleaning, and dishes, walked side by side with the first lady before taking a position in the center of the East Room.
## [Watch here:](https://substack.com/redirect/ee5480dd-b944-4763-9c4b-dbf76dda60a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ee5480dd-b944-4763-9c4b-dbf76dda60a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/ee5480dd-b944-4763-9c4b-dbf76dda60a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **What it said:** After scanning the audience, Figure 03 said "thank you, first lady Melania Trump, for inviting me to the White House. It is an honor to be at Fostering the Future Together's global coalition inaugural meeting. I'm Figure 03, a humanoid built for the United States of America. I am grateful to be part of this historic movement to empower children with technology and education." It then offered greetings in 10 other languages before retracing its steps back down the red carpet.
* **Why it matters:** The first lady thanked the robot, saying "it's fair to state, you are my first American-made humanoid guest in the White House." Figure AI CEO Brett Adcock said on social media he was "proud to see F.03 make history as the first humanoid robot in the White House," with the Sunnyvale startup competing with Boston Dynamics, Elon Musk's Tesla, and Chinese companies in building human-like robots.

# **U.S., Israel face growing cost imbalance as Iran 's cheap drones drain expensive interceptors despite 90% success rate**
More than 90% of Iranian projectiles have been intercepted during the war, with U.S. forces destroying over 9,000 enemy targets and Iran's attacks down roughly 90%, **[according to a JINSA report and White House statements.](https://substack.com/redirect/dbed9f72-e6af-4f5f-821c-f7381deb45f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** However, experts warn Iran's $30,000 drones are draining interceptors costing millions of dollars, with JINSA's Ari Cicurel saying "overall high missile and drone interception rates have been important but only tell part of the story."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dbed9f72-e6af-4f5f-821c-f7381deb45f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** Gulf states have depleted massive portions of their interceptor inventories--Bahrain may have expended up to 87% of Patriot missiles, UAE and Kuwait roughly 75%, and Qatar around 40%--while Israel shows signs of rationing by not intercepting certain threats. Middle East expert Danny Citrinowicz warned "the Iranians are launching drones that cost around $30,000, and we are using missiles that cost millions," adding "it's easier and quicker to produce missiles than it is to build interceptors."
* **The challenge:** Iran has shifted to smaller, frequent attacks to maintain constant pressure while draining defensive resources, using advanced drones including fiber-optic guided models immune to jamming and jet-powered variants. Cicurel said "the architecture has held, but the trajectory is moving in the wrong direction," with the key question being "whether Iran can produce missiles faster than we can produce interceptors."

It is an honor to be at Fostering the Future Together's global coalition inaugural meeting. I'm Figure 03, a humanoid built for the United States of America. I am grateful to be part of this historic movement to empower children with technology and education." It then offered greetings in 10 other languages before retracing its steps back down the red carpet. Why it matters: The first lady thanked the robot, saying "it's fair to state, you are my first American-made humanoid guest in the White House." Figure AI CEO Brett Adcock said on social media he was "proud to see F.03 make history as the first humanoid robot in the White House," with the Sunnyvale startup competing with Boston Dynamics, Elon Musk's Tesla, and Chinese companies in building human-like robots. U.S., Israel face growing cost imbalance as Iran 's cheap drones drain expensive interceptors despite 90% success rate More than 90% of Iranian projectiles have been intercepted during the war, with U.S. forces destroying over 9,000 enemy targets and Iran's attacks down roughly 90%, However, experts warn Iran's $30,000 drones are draining interceptors costing millions of dollars, with JINSA's Ari Cicurel saying "overall high missile and drone interception rates have been important but only tell part of the story." | | ---|---|--- Why it matters: Gulf states have depleted massive portions of their interceptor inventories--Bahrain may have expended up to 87% of Patriot missiles, UAE and Kuwait roughly 75%, and Qatar around 40%--while Israel shows signs of rationing by not intercepting certain threats. Middle East expert Danny Citrinowicz warned "the Iranians are launching drones that cost around $30,000, and we are using missiles that cost millions," adding "it's easier and quicker to produce missiles than it is to build interceptors." The challenge: Iran has shifted to smaller, frequent attacks to maintain constant pressure while draining defensive resources, using advanced drones including fiber-optic guided models immune to jamming and jet-powered variants. Cicurel said "the architecture has held, but the trajectory is moving in the wrong direction," with the key question being "whether Iran can produce missiles faster than we can produce interceptors." His family terrorized for years, children taunted with slurs in the streets, living under police protection for nearly a decade. This isn't a scene from some distant war zone. **This happened in Bradford, England – to Nissar Hussain.** **His only "crime"? Leaving Islam and embracing Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior.** For 17 years, Nissar endured relentless persecution from his former community. The Church of England? _**SILENT.**_ Not one bishop stood with him or his family. **But Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member, refused to stand by. clean_body: The Far-Left STILL wants to see lives destroyed beyond repair | | | | Dear Faithful Friend, Imagine this: A man steps outside his own home in a quiet neighborhood. Suddenly, violence erupts, his kneecap shattered in a brutal attack. His car torched. His family terrorized for years, children taunted with slurs in the streets, living under police protection for nearly a decade. This isn't a scene from some distant war zone. This happened in Bradford, England – to Nissar Hussain. His only "crime"? Leaving Islam and embracing Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. For 17 years, Nissar endured relentless persecution from his former community. The Church of England? SILENT. Not one bishop stood with him or his family. But Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member, refused to stand by. We brought Nissar here to the U.S. to help him share his story, and he is now fighting back boldly – in part by pursuing a groundbreaking legal case against 11 countries that still mandate death for apostasy. Nissar's story is heartbreaking, but it's not isolated. Over 380 million Christians face severe persecution globally, and the numbers are growing. In Iran, 254 believers were arrested in 2025 alone for simply practicing their faith, escalating further amid the regime's war on Christians. In Nigeria, thousands have been slaughtered by Islamist militants: entire villages massacred, girls held captive for years, all because they refused to deny Christ. In Pakistan, blasphemy laws are twisted to destroy Christian lives. In North Korea, owning a Bible can mean a lifetime in a labor camp. It is for all of these reasons that Save the Persecuted Christians is relentlessly educating Americans and rallying the faithful to recognize the threat before it takes deeper root here. A powerful example: Our ongoing education and advocacy efforts helped fuel the overwhelming success on March 3, when 95% of Texas Republican primary voters stood up and voted to ban Sharia law – sending a clear, faithful message: We will not let this ideology gain a foothold in America and threaten our freedoms or our persecuted brothers and sisters in Christ. The threat is real. Persecution that starts overseas doesn't always stay there. We must be extra vigilant, and we need your help right now to keep pushing back. Your gift, especially a monthly commitment through The Defenders Guild, multiplies our impact and sustains the fight against this growing evil. Paul wrote in Galatians 6:2, “Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” That is our mandate as the Body of Christ. The Church must rise in one spirit, refusing silence in the face of darkness. Thank you for your faithfulness and courage in this hour. Ken Burns here, friend. I’ve said this before and it’s now more relevant than ever: The power rests in our hands to secure the future of the Senate.
**_[I have more to say, but if you want to use that power in your own hands, and have a few bucks to spare, please consider donating to Roy Cooper’s campaign today. Across this country, people are feeling the strain in ways that don’t always make the history books – but shape lives all the same. The cost of groceries that are too high. A life-saving prescription that forces a difficult choice. A paycheck that doesn’t just stretch as far as it once did.
These are the quiet pressures that define a moment.

Roy Cooper has spent much of his life as a public servant working to ease those burdens.
Not seeking attention, but doing the work. Expanding access to affordable health care. Investing in public schools. Defending the idea that government, at its best, is not distant – but present, steady, and accountable to the people it serves.
It is the kind of leadership that rarely makes noise. But over time, it leaves a mark.

There are those who would take the state in a different direction – who see division as a strategy, who mistake power for purpose. They are organized. They are well-funded by dark money groups.
**_[We can beat them back. This work matters and we won’t stop fighting. So please, will you chip in now to help elect Roy Cooper for the U.S. Senate?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/7523?t=8&akid=829%2E124072%2E5rrKU5)_**

History has been written in moments like this – when people choose not to sit back, but to take part.
If you can, _[**give today**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/7523?t=10&akid=829%2E124072%2E5rrKU5)_. Help ensure that the next chapter of North Carolina reflects the very best of what this state has always tried to be.
Thank you for doing your part,

Ken Burns

We are in the middle of Senate District convention season, and I have been reflecting on Kelly’s first political campaign for the Minnesota State House. In February of 2018, I accompanied Kelly on precinct caucus night in Minnetonka. She walked into a classroom where she introduced herself and spoke about why she was running. One man in the crowd listened politely, then leaned in and said:
“You seem like a nice lady. But will you be tough enough when the Republicans come after you?
Peter, we all know the answer to that question — Kelly Morrison is pretty damn tough.
I was with her at the Whipple Federal Building this winter. And I have never been more proud than when she marched past the protestors, past the security guards, and right up to the armed ICE agents and demanded to be let in to conduct oversight.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
