While we were in Court, Judicial Watch filed a new lawsuit against the federal government for gain-of-function (GOF) funding proposals prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. As you know, COVID-19 was also an election integrity crisis with many states using the pandemic as a reason to extend ballot counting after Election Day for weeks... We want to find out what the Deep State operatives knew.... And did our government help fund research which led to the pandemic? Our new lawsuit aims to find out and | ** We are using the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) to seek records on GOF funding proposals submitted to the Biological Technologies Office of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) before December 2019. Senator Rand Paul has previously written that at least 15 federal agencies knew from the beginning of the pandemic that EcoHealth Alliance and the Chinese-based Wuhan Institute of Virology were seeking federal funding in 2018 to create a virus genetically similar if not identical to COVID-19. We have reason to believe GOF proposals were active in the Defense Department’s pipeline prior to the pandemic. Our lawsuit intends to find out what these proposals entailed. Judicial Watch has been a national leader in exposing government secrets about COVID-19 and Thank you for fighting for government transparency with Judicial Watch. | | Hi, This is Brigadier General James Emory Mace, U.S. Army (Retired). _**Today, I write to you not as a soldier... _but as a father._**_ I’m a Vietnam War Veteran and **Purple Heart Medal** recipient. I’ve worn the uniform. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

We maintain our strength in order to deter and defend against aggression -- to preserve freedom and peace_.” Rob said pointedly, _“_ We broke that commitment in the joint attack with Israel on the sovereign nation of Iran. | Peter,

I refuse to simply sit and wait for the next gun tragedy. We’ve seen too many mass shootings, too many lives lost, and too many gun manufacturers getting rich off of our pain.

**That’s why I recently introduced a bill to ban high-capacity magazines in Michigan, because weapons of mass destruction should not be on our streets.**

The fact is, wealthy gun manufacturers don’t care about our safety. They continue to push products that are designed for mass destruction, all while making millions off the destruction of communities.

_I say it’s time to hold them accountable._

My bill takes aim at these high-capacity magazines, which are often used in the deadliest mass shootings. We need to prevent these weapons from falling into the wrong hands and stop mass shootings before they happen.

I’m asking for your help today. The fight for gun safety isn’t over, and I need you by my side.

subject: President Trump just voted by mail
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
President Trump has been railing against mail-in voting for YEARS.
So imagine our surprise when, just this week, he voted in a special election in Florida...by mail.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
If it’s good enough for you, Mr. President, it’s good enough for all of us.
I’m Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Read.
President Trump and his MAGA allies are hypocritically coming after mail-in voting for one simple reason: They want to make it harder for regular people to participate in our democracy.
As Secretary of State, I’m standing up to him by fighting to protect the right of all Oregon voters to vote from home.
But I need to know you're with me: If you support my efforts to expand vote-by-mail access, please consider donating to help me continue fighting today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
In Oregon, we’ve proven for more than 25 years that vote-by-mail works. It’s secure, accurate, and accessible — and Oregonians of all political backgrounds overwhelmingly support it. Fraud is essentially nonexistent, participation is among the highest in the country, and our paper ballots provide a fully auditable trail.
And now we know that President Trump agrees!
As your Secretary of State, I’ve pledged that Oregon will stand up to any unconstitutional attempt to take away our right to vote by mail. But to fight back, I need your support.
Will you chip in today to help defend Oregon’s vote-by-mail system and protect our democracy? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
Thanks for your support,
Tobias Read

That's why I'm the only Democrat that can beat Mike Rogers

---
# ["Independent magic" is going to decide this race](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=192241197&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkyMjQxMTk3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzQ1NTQzODMsImV4cCI6MTc3NzE0NjM4MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.B8c1GYL_Cy_p6RHUg9ZWCOpfmuw6uyxnGXzdhIuoKec)
### That's why I'm the only Democrat that can beat Mike Rogers
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Mar 26
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..SeelfKQPwn9yh0kFW-c9yQWwOkaUF1TM2AZCWCFTx1o?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/independent-magic-is-going-to-decide?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
There's a phrase that I've heard pundits use multiple times when they talk about this race and my campaign:
**Independent magic.**
That phrase means more to me than almost anything else that's been said about this race, because of one simple fact:
_**That 's how you win in Michigan.**_
When we get to Election Day and voters are casting their ballots to decide who their next senator is, it's going to come down to the wire. Michigan's Senate election in 2024 was decided by just _0.3%_ of the vote - and poll after poll tells us that this year is going to be just as close.
And when the margins are that slim, there's one key demographic that it all comes down to: _independent voters._
They are the ones who are going to decide if we elect a Democrat who will fight for Michigan workers, or a MAGA candidate who represents the worst of politics. That's the truth. And the other truth is: None of my primary opponents come close to me with independents.
**I 'm leading Mike Rogers by 1 point with registered voters - and when it comes to definite voters, that jumps up to **_**6 points**_**. That 's huge.**
What it comes down to is that voters, whether Democrats or independents, know what we've been saying all along.
Michiganders can count on me to stand up to the status quo, fight for them, and win for them- because it's what I've been doing throughout my career.
It's what I did as President Obama's Chief of Staff on the Auto Rescue Task Force during the Great Recession when we helped save 200,000 auto jobs in Michigan. It's what I've been doing as House rep for MI-11 in Congress, where I'm one of the most effective Democrats in the chamber
**And it 's what I'll keep doing as Michigan's next senator.**
That's what "independent magic" is all about. And it's why I'm the only Democrat in this race with a real shot at defeating Mike Rogers and keeping this seat blue.
With grit and determination,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/8a222eff-1c6b-4139-b240-58807400acec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Friend,
Facing bias and discrimination is nothing new to me.
I've faced it almost my entire career, whether it's on the paycheck or on the ballot. And the sad truth is that many women can say the same.
Today is Equal Pay Day, an extremely important reminder that we're still struggling to overcome the inequality between men and women when it comes to pay.
Recent reports show that women earn ~80% of what a man does.
The effects of this extend far beyond just a paycheck, and it contributes to other workplace inequalities as well.
Friend, even in this Democratic primary, the biases that discredit women and their achievements have been used against me.
But like the countless women who continue to fight in the face of adversity, I won't let this stop me.
I'm ready to fight to deliver results for our communities and vote for Medicare for All, push for a Green New Deal, and abolish ICE. But I can't do it without you. Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.

This shouldn’t be ignored, friend. Last year, **the Trump administration cut nearly 30% of the workforce and slashed hundreds of millions of dollars** from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) – the federal agency that helps states protect election systems from hacking and foreign interference. At the same time, experts are warning that foreign adversaries – including nation-state hackers – are again probing U.S. election infrastructure for weaknesses. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128125713/610324411/38783915?refcode=em-3.26.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzEzNjJkNS00YzI5LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RFRN0OFL2IsQDbZ3ynHu_-D1rO4QfXB5kya4G3OF_DY=) **The lead U.S. cyber agency is stretched thin as Iran hacking threat escalates**

Secretaries of State are an important line of defense to keep our election systems secure, but they also depend on federal coordination to defend voting infrastructure from foreign attacks.
**With the 2026 midterms approaching, we can’t afford to fall behind.**
That’s why Democratic Secretaries of State are working to ensure our elections remain secure, resilient, and protected from cyber threats.

* **Protect Privacy:** Oppose the expansion of federal surveillance at the local level.
* **Defend Protest:** Ensure that local law enforcement protects the First Amendment right to dissent, even when the federal government calls it "sedition."
* **Audit Federal Overreach:** Prevent local resources from being diverted into unconstitutional federal "security" programs.

Hi there,
After serving our country for 35 years in the Navy, I was removed from my position by Pete Hegseth without reason.
I spent my entire life in service to this country, always putting the mission and the people above myself. But when I was forced out, I had a choice: go out quietly, or find a way to keep serving.
I’ve always lived by three simple ideals: honor, integrity, and respect. That’s why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s first district. If you believe that’s what we need in Washington right now, please consider splitting $20 between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]
BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR TO MY CAMPAIGN TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]
The day I was removed from my position, I was forced to leave behind my life’s work. I never went back to the Pentagon or wore the uniform again.
But this story isn’t just about me. Throughout the first year of Donald Trump’s second term, every woman serving as a three or four-star admiral in the Navy has been fired, forced out, or reassigned. This wasn’t an isolated incident. It’s a pattern.
When leadership decisions are driven by politics instead of integrity, our families, communities, and nation pay the price.

Peter,
Florida held a handful of elections on Tuesday in red districts that no one expected Democrats to compete in.
Dems flipped two crucial seats: one of those being the state house district where Trump is registered to vote that encompasses Mar-a-Lago.
The fallout has been fierce.
And now Florida GOP Reps and strategists are now sounding off about the risk of Trump's push to rig districts backfiring on them this November:
It's a "slippery slope" according to one GOP Rep. "I've been around enough to know it can come back and bite you."
"I don't like this redistricting stuff" said another state lawmaker.

This race will probably be the closest in the state, and far-right House Republicans are making no secret that they’re desperate to get involved to flip this seat. = | = While Dillan Vancil backed ICE's raids in Minnesota — and even called for them to come here — Eric Sorensen was busy getting results for Central and Northwest Illinois. Since he was elected, Eric has helped revitalize communities across the district, supporting investments in local manufacturing jobs, law enforcement, and education. He’s shown us he’s a true bipartisan leader. Eric’s goal is the same as mine: improving lives for the people of Illinois. Unfortunately, the far right is trying to polarize and mislead Illinoisans into believing otherwise. Let’s show them we see right through this charade and help Eric push back against these smears. = = Thank you, Peter. Your support will make a real difference. Take care, JB Pritzker | Eric Sorensen is a meteorologist born and raised in Rockford, IL representing IL-17 in Congress. He’s seen firsthand the importance of establishing trust with the community, and he’s determined to use his expertise as a climate communicator to fight for Illinoisans on environmental justice and more in Washington. Friend, Did you know that the majority of members of Congress are millionaires? https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
You open an app on your phone. You visit a few websites on your computer. Even when you think you’re not revealing anything, your data is often being tracked.
Those apps and websites can amass information about you — what you’ve bought, where you are, your habits, your health — and sell it to third-party data brokers that build a whole profile on you.
Luckily, California has robust privacy laws that give us control over our data. But there is no such federal protection — and the Trump administration knows that.
Right now, the federal government is allowed to buy and use vast sets of data about Americans, with no limits, oversight, or accountability.
This mass surveillance is dangerous for democracy.
That’s why I’m strongly urging Congress to take action and limit the federal government’s ability to deploy mass surveillance on the American people.
If you agree we need action, please add your name to my petition today so we can show strong grassroots support. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/YSJyTXAZvkaZuQl4coeiWw2?contactdata=vzaa3KWtffe6SIcvNvKOwACygUHqYKch60KRtyizaUjsLHJ7qjnXKb+cK5KmWKEbqaIJ9tTNlgTURdMvLRGg8vjdfSPemZ7RC1GXCgSSCx1Nwnfus9zhmNu30bBq6qBnXzrLaLLa/9EteJjv9NsYhcVVTvnigxhZ2ecC+RyuP6k=]

This administration is already pushing the limits to target immigrants, the LGBTQ+ community, abortion providers — anyone who doesn’t align with their extreme agenda. The time is NOW for Congress to meaningfully protect our data privacy.
Bottom line: If the federal government wants to access our digital data, it should be required to get a warrant. And there should be oversight, transparency, and accountability.
If you’re with me on this, please sign my petition today. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/YSJyTXAZvkaZuQl4coeiWw2?contactdata=vzaa3KWtffe6SIcvNvKOwACygUHqYKch60KRtyizaUjsLHJ7qjnXKb+cK5KmWKEbqaIJ9tTNlgTURdMvLRGg8vjdfSPemZ7RC1GXCgSSCx1Nwnfus9zhmNu30bBq6qBnXzrLaLLa/9EteJjv9NsYhcVVTvnigxhZ2ecC+RyuP6k=]
Then, call the U.S. Capitol switchboard at (202) 224-3121 and urge your representatives to take action.
Thanks for speaking out with me on this critical issue.
—Rob

body:
https://www.frostforcongress.com/ [https://www.frostforcongress.com/]
Peter,
I want to share a campaign update because there’s a lot going on.
First: we’re officially qualifying for the ballot through petitions [https://www.frostforcongress.com/petition] .
In Florida, candidates can either pay a massive filing fee or earn their place on the ballot by collecting signatures from voters. We’re choosing the people-powered path . That means talking to voters, organizing our community, and educating voters.
Over the next few weeks, I’ll be out across Central Florida alongside volunteers collecting petitions at events, neighborhoods, and community spaces. If you haven’t signed yet – or want to help us collect – this is the moment to get involved.
At the same time, we’re facing a serious challenge.
Governor DeSantis and Florida Republicans are preparing for a Special Session on redistricting the week of April 20. That means they’re trying to redraw the congressional map mid-decade to hold onto power.
Let’s be clear: this is an attempt to rig the system. If they succeed, it won’t just impact our district – it could shape control of Congress for years to come.
That’s why we’re preparing on every front: organizing, building coalitions, and working with legal and community partners to push back.
And we’re continuing to invest in the next generation of organizers. Applications for our Democracy Summer Fellowship are now open , [https://democracy-summer.breezy.hr/p/e0e26de21e61-rep-maxwell-frost-fl-10] and we’re building our largest class yet to register voters, mobilize young people, and strengthen this movement from the ground up.
All of this is happening as we approach a critical end-of-quarter fundraising deadline on March 31st .
In moments like this, resources matter. Whether it’s scaling our petition effort, expanding outreach, or preparing for redistricting — we have to be ready to move quickly.
If you’re able, will you chip in before our March 31st EOQ deadline?
👉 CONTRIBUTE ONLINE HERE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mafnewsletter]
What gives me hope is this: people are stepping up.
Volunteers collecting petitions. Young people organizing their communities. Neighbors coming together to protect each other and our democracy.
That’s how we win – not just elections, but the future.
Be sure to read the rest of this newsletter for ways to get involved.
With love and gratitude,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92662/images/maxwell%20signature.png]
Maxwell Alejandro Frost
U.S. Representative (FL-10)
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92662/images/IMG_7068%20%282%29.jpeg]
Congressman Frost & volunteers.
Help Get Maxwell on the Ballot – Sign Our Petition!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92662/images/signal-2026-03-26-141712.jpeg] We’re taking the people-powered path to the ballot — and we need your help.
Any registered Florida voter can sign a petition to help Maxwell qualify for the 2026 Election. We’re working to collect 4,000+ petitions , and every single signature brings us closer.
Please also share with friends and family — your network can make a real impact.
Our deadline to submit petitions is May 11 , so timing is critical.
SIGN A PETITION TODAY [https://www.frostforcongress.com/petition]
Apply for Democracy Summer!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92662/images/Democracy%20Summer%20Application.png] Want to make a real impact this summer? Democracy Summer is our paid organizing fellowship bringing together young people across Central Florida to do the work that wins elections — registering voters, collecting petitions, and organizing in their communities.
If you’re ready to step up, gain real experience, and be part of something bigger, this is your moment.
Applications close April 15.
APPLY TODAY [https://www.frostforcongress.com/democracysummer]

clean_body: [] Peter, I want to share a campaign update because there’s a lot going on. First: we’re officially qualifying for the ballot through petitions [] . In Florida, candidates can either pay a massive filing fee or earn their place on the ballot by collecting signatures from voters. We’re choosing the people-powered path . That means talking to voters, organizing our community, and educating voters. Over the next few weeks, I’ll be out across Central Florida alongside volunteers collecting petitions at events, neighborhoods, and community spaces. If you haven’t signed yet – or want to help us collect – this is the moment to get involved. At the same time, we’re facing a serious challenge. Governor DeSantis and Florida Republicans are preparing for a Special Session on redistricting the week of April 20. That means they’re trying to redraw the congressional map mid-decade to hold onto power. Let’s be clear: this is an attempt to rig the system. If they succeed, it won’t just impact our district – it could shape control of Congress for years to come. That’s why we’re preparing on every front: organizing, building coalitions, and working with legal and community partners to push back. And we’re continuing to invest in the next generation of organizers. Applications for our Democracy Summer Fellowship are now open , [] and we’re building our largest class yet to register voters, mobilize young people, and strengthen this movement from the ground up. All of this is happening as we approach a critical end-of-quarter fundraising deadline on March 31st . In moments like this, resources matter. Whether it’s scaling our petition effort, expanding outreach, or preparing for redistricting — we have to be ready to move quickly. If you’re able, will you chip in before our March 31st EOQ deadline? 👉 CONTRIBUTE ONLINE HERE [] What gives me hope is this: people are stepping up. Volunteers collecting petitions. **This Tuesday, March 31st, our campaign has to publicly report all of our fundraising data to the Federal Election Commission (FEC).**
Each FEC deadline is our chance to show the strength of our campaign, but this one is even more important because it’s our first since our primary election victory and the first of this critical election year.
What we’re able to raise by midnight on March 31st will become public, which means we have just a few days left to close the gap, hit our fundraising goal, and put us on the path for a big win in November.

#### _**Cliff 's Note**_: Let's stop pretending. When the same names keep circling the same scandals, the same power networks, the same exploitation--it's not coincidence. It's a pattern. And we need to call it what it is: predators protecting predators.
#### If you're tired of the sanitized version of reality, that's exactly why we do this.

* * *
_**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
Jeffrey Epstein did not fall from the sky.
He didn't materialize out of nowhere--a lone monster, a one-off aberration, a story that begins and ends with one deeply sick man and his private island. That is the story some very powerful people very badly want you to believe. It is not true. Epstein was a product, a symptom, and ultimately a mirror--held up to a class of men who have spent decades operating on the same foundational belief: that the rules everyone else lives by simply do not apply to them.
Not the laws of nations. Not the laws of decency. Not, in the end, even the laws of basic human conscience.
We have a word for what Epstein did to the young girls he trafficked, abused, and lent out to other powerful men like party favors. **We call it predation**. It is the correct word. He identified vulnerable targets. He groomed them. He extracted what he wanted from them. He discarded them. He used his wealth and his network as a shield, and when that shield finally--partially, incompletely --failed, he died in a federal facility under circumstances that remain, to put it generously, unresolved.

Call them what they are. Call them the Predator Class.
The term is not new. Serious thinkers--economists, journalists, historians watching the arc of late-stage capitalism bend toward something ugly--have used this language for years. But it has not yet broken into mainstream discourse with the force it deserves. We still reach for softer words. The "ultra-wealthy." The "billionaire class." The "one percent." These phrases are accurate but they are bloodless. They describe an economic category. They do not describe a behavior. And behavior is exactly what we need to be talking about.
Because the behavior is consistent. It is the same behavior, expressed at different scales.

Elon Musk does not simply run companies. He manipulates markets with a tweet--pumping a cryptocurrency, tanking a stock, moving billions of dollars of other people's money with a joke or a mood -- and faces no meaningful consequence. He has been handed the keys to the United States federal government's financial infrastructure by a president he helped install, and he is using those keys to dismantle agencies, fire inspectors, and gut the oversight mechanisms that exist specifically to keep men like him in check. This is predation. It is the extraction of value from systems that took generations to build, executed with the casual confidence of a man who has never once been told no in a way that actually stuck.

And they have learned, over the course of the last several decades, that the most powerful tool available to them is not money, though they have plenty of that. It is the fragmentation of language. So let's do that.

Not as a rhetorical flourish or hyperbole, but because it is a precise, accurate description. It's taxonomy. We are labeling them what they really are: predators, and by definition, a threat.
What Epstein did to those girls--the grooming, the exploitation, the network of powerful men who benefited and protected him--is not a metaphor for what this class does to the rest of us. It is the same instinct, the same calculus, the same fundamental belief expressed in different arenas. That some people exist to be used. That power confers the right to take. That accountability is for other people.

Start using it. Predator Class. Say it until it sticks. Say it until it shows up in headlines, in dinner table conversations, in the framing of every story about who is doing what to whom and why.

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: No more blank checks....
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
In business and in life there’s one rule everyone understands: no one gets a blank check.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| |

In business and in life there’s one rule everyone understands:
**No one gets a blank check.**
Not families balancing their household budgets.
Not business owners making payroll.
Not anyone who understands that every dollar has to be earned and accounted for.But in Johnson County government, that standard has slipped.
At a recent February 12th meeting, Commission Chair Mike Kelly, when discussing a no-bid contract extension, said:
_“The amount of questions I have asked indicates I am struggling with this too... but at the same time, I see myself as a policy maker and I trust our team, understanding this is a tool the team says they need...”_
Let’s pause on that.
When something doesn’t feel right... when questions remain unanswered... when even leadership admits they are “struggling” because they aren't sure exactly what the deliverable or outcome expected is...
That is exactly the moment to slow down, demand clarity, and protect taxpayer dollars.Instead, what we’re seeing is a willingness to **defer, approve, and move forward anyway.** That’s how you end up with:
* A **$1.9 billion budget** , the largest in county history
* Continued **property tax increases**
* And decisions that feel more like a **blank check for government** than responsible stewardship
*
That’s not leadership. That’s passing the responsibility on and expecting taxpayers to cover the cost.
I’m running for Johnson County Commission Chair because I believe we need to restore a simple principle:
**If you wouldn’t approve it in your own business or home you shouldn’t approve it in government.**
As a business owner, I’ve had to make tough calls when something didn’t add up. You don’t move forward just because someone says, “we need it.” You ask the hard questions. You demand accountability. And if the answers aren't there, you don’t sign the check, YOU SAY NO.
Johnson County deserves that level of discipline and respect for your tax dollars.
But bringing that change will take all of us.
This campaign is about standing up for taxpayers and pushing back on a system that has grown too comfortable spending without limits.
I’m asking you to be part of that effort.
Your contribution, whether it’s $50, $100, or $250 will help us reach more voters, challenge the status quo, and build the momentum we need to win.
---
| [DONATE TODAY!](https://kcforjoco.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d540da3225ec5b2797f3018d2&id=ba9ff03998&e=7320325a61)
---
| |

Together, we can end blank-check government and restore accountability to Johnson County.
Thank you for standing with me.
Sincerely,
**Karen Crnkovich**
Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

### One year after State Auditor Matt Dunlap's 2024 audit revealed systemic weaknesses and almost non-existent controls on Mills Administration spending, very little has changed in state government.
Mar 26

The Mills Administration's mismanaged spending is once again in the spotlight after another bombshell audit revealed a $6 billion web of sloppy bookkeeping, missed deadlines, and "material noncompliance" with federal law.
* State Auditor Auditor Matthew Dunlap's team identified **19 "material weaknesses"**--the gold medal of accounting failures. These represent cases where the state's "controls" are so weak they can't even prevent or detect a major mistake before it happens.
* **The Dead Participation:** In the SNAP program, auditors found that benefits were issued to **29 cases** more than 75 days after the client had died. Seven single-member households had **$4,335** in EBT purchase activity recorded after the client passed away.
* **The $1.6 Billion Free-for-All:** The state blew through **$1.6 billion** in contracts while ignoring its own rules. Nearly two-thirds of tested contracts weren't signed on time, with some signed nearly a year after the contract started.
* **Accounting Voodoo:** The state's new Paid Family and Medical Leave Fund was an absolute disaster, initially missing **$47 million** in receivables. Meanwhile, the state had to fix a **$119.3 million** tax-reporting blunder.
* **The Medicaid Black Hole:** Despite handling **$3.4 billion** in federal funds, the state didn't finish a single one of its 88 required nursing home audits.
* Known "questioned costs"--taxpayer money potentially spent in the wrong places--totaled **$657,755** , but the audit warns the actual number could be much higher since many errors were "undeterminable"
* State agencies largely agreed with the findings but pointed to "staff turnover" and "lack of resources" as the reason for the chaos.

Photo: Matt Dunlap on The Robinson Report
At the top of the wild breaches of basic good governance identified by the Office of State Auditor (OSA): Maine failed to complete a single one of the 88 nursing facility audits due in fiscal year 2025 even as $382.4 million in federal and state Medicaid money flowed to nursing homes.
That's according to the state's annual single audit, prepared by the OSA and released by State Auditor Matt Dunlap, a longtime Democrat official who is currently a candidate for the Democratic nomination in Maine's Second Congressional District race.
That finding was among the biggest in a series of fiscal failures flagged by the Office of the State Auditor in the single annual report released Thursday evening.
The flubbed nursing home audits were part of broader trend of control failures observed statewide for yet another year: auditors also said they could not determine whether Maine's Medicaid utilization-control program was complete across a $3.2 billion program serving about 10,600 providers, and they found procurement failures across roughly $1.6 billion in contract-related payments.
The nursing-facility finding was not a one-year miss.
Auditors traced it back through every fiscal year from 2018 through 2025. The report says Maine completed 61 desk reviews -- i.e. phone call surveys in place of site visits -- during fiscal 2025, but all of them were for prior years, leaving the entire current-year population of required reviews undone when auditors tested the program in October 2025.
The Office of the State Auditor recommended that departments "enhance oversight to ensure that federal program cash balances are tracked by program in accordance with federal requirements". While the state provided unmodified opinions on its basic financial statements, the volume of internal control failures suggests a strained administrative infrastructure struggling to keep pace with federal mandates.
The procurement finding was the audit's other statewide alarm bell.
Perhaps most striking was the state's handling of its $1.6 billion procurement and contract payment portfolio. Auditors tested 57 active contracts and found that 36 were not signed at least 14 days prior to the start date, as required by policy. In some instances, contracts and justification forms were signed up to 360 days after the work had supposedly commenced.
To translate that from CPA speak: The Mills Administration is brazenly disregarding the rules for handing out taxpayer cash for good and services. Money is leaving state accounts before contracts are signed, non-transparent processes are being used in ways that violate state policies, and the state continues to use no-bid contracts with little regard for transparency or the law.
The Single Audit Report identified 62 separate deficiencies in internal controls over federal compliance. Of these, 19 were classified as material weaknesses, the most severe category of reporting failure. The audit led to qualified opinions on 10 major federal programs, including Medicaid, SNAP, and Child Nutrition, due to material noncompliance with federal requirements.
Every material control issue involving federally funded projects raises the prospect that the Trump Administration could claw back that funding.

#### Maine Audit Uncovers 'Brazen' Disregard for Taxpayer Cash, Kids in Danger
The mismanagement has even trickled down to the state's most vulnerable, an area of the state policy that has received considerable attention due to the stunningly high rate of child fatalities in state care. Auditors found children were placed in homes that did not satisfy required abuse-and-neglect registry checks. In one finding, auditors said five clients were placed in a resource family home where the foster or adoptive parent did not satisfactorily meet the registry check, producing $7,629 in questioned foster care costs and $42,689 in questioned adoption-assistance costs. The audit says two of those five children were later removed from the home after the checks were completed.
Auditors also found a separate case in which a prospective foster parent failed the check and the home still received $12,566 in federal foster care benefits on behalf of two clients, and another two clients who had been deemed ineligible kept receiving payments because of a child-welfare system conversion problem.
A separate foster care finding showed the same pattern of weak controls after placement. Auditors tested 60 cases and found 36 children did not receive the required level-of-care assessment within 90 days, with delays ranging from 11 to 302 days. They also found one child's level-of-care designation was automatically changed by the child welfare information system under draft policies that had not been formally approved, generating $3,003 in questioned costs. Taken together, the audit describes a state government that kept moving money while basic oversight, procurement and child-safety controls lagged behind.
Taken together, the audit describes a state government that kept moving money while basic oversight, procurement, and child-safety controls lagged behind.
The audit also captured a blunt management response from DHHS. In the procurement finding, the department said "there is not a requirement to provide documentation" that personnel assertions on procurement justification forms are accurate. In other words, DHHS argued there's no requirement for them to tell the truth when they're directing taxpayer-funded contracts via no-bid contracts.
Auditors rejected that argument, writing that without documentation supporting those assertions, "the best value for the State cannot be ensured." The same statewide procurement finding says the comprehensive purchasing policy and operations manual had not been formally updated since 2015.

#### Accounting Errors and Procurement Risks
The report detailed significant accounting lapses within the newly established Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) Fund -- the Democrat plan to levy a one-percent tax on paychecks so that workers can get paid vacations for pretty much any reason. Auditors found that accounts receivable were initially understated by $47 million, while $7.1 million in software expenditures were erroneously expensed rather than capitalized.
That's an inauspicious beginning for a program that hasn't even started providing the alleged benefits to Maine's workers.
Further fiscal friction was noted in individual income tax reporting. A methodology error resulted in a $119.3 million overstatement of taxes receivable and deferred inflows, requiring a retroactive restatement of the state's beginning net position.
#### Big Picture: Nothing has changed since last years single annual report exposed more than $2.1 billion in spending at risk for fraud and corruption due to terrible internal controls.
The last state audit, [published just one year ago](https://substack.com/redirect/2b8f5511-616c-4e92-b995-af9d6262afef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), said taxpayers were exposed to major financial risk because the state lacked basic oversight over contract spending and procurement controls. The audit found **$2.1 billion in FY2024 contract payments** were made under a system the audit found lacked adequate supervisory controls.
Last year's report reviewed **45 procurement actions** and found **no documentation of cost analysis in any of them**. They also found that **16 of 31 sole-source contracts** lacked documentation of the required "reasonable investigation." In one case, a sole-source contract was approved only after the work had already been completed.
In the audit published last year, auditors also found evidence that low-cost contracts were being used to avoid competitive bidding, a practice known as "stacking" contracts. In one example, a department awarded **seven concurrent low-cost service contracts** to the same vendor in a single year, which the article describes as a way to dodge oversight.
The Mills Administration never commented publicly on the 2024 annual report and there's no evidence that any state employee was disciplined for the financial mismanagement.

In some instances, contracts and justification forms were signed up to 360 days after the work had supposedly commenced. To translate that from CPA speak: The Mills Administration is brazenly disregarding the rules for handing out taxpayer cash for good and services. Money is leaving state accounts before contracts are signed, non-transparent processes are being used in ways that violate state policies, and the state continues to use no-bid contracts with little regard for transparency or the law. The Single Audit Report identified 62 separate deficiencies in internal controls over federal compliance. Of these, 19 were classified as material weaknesses, the most severe category of reporting failure. The audit led to qualified opinions on 10 major federal programs, including Medicaid, SNAP, and Child Nutrition, due to material noncompliance with federal requirements. Every material control issue involving federally funded projects raises the prospect that the Trump Administration could claw back that funding. Maine Audit Uncovers 'Brazen' Disregard for Taxpayer Cash, Kids in Danger The mismanagement has even trickled down to the state's most vulnerable, an area of the state policy that has received considerable attention due to the stunningly high rate of child fatalities in state care. Auditors found children were placed in homes that did not satisfy required abuse-and-neglect registry checks. In one finding, auditors said five clients were placed in a resource family home where the foster or adoptive parent did not satisfactorily meet the registry check, producing $7,629 in questioned foster care costs and $42,689 in questioned adoption-assistance costs. The audit says two of those five children were later removed from the home after the checks were completed. Auditors also found a separate case in which a prospective foster parent failed the check and the home still received $12,566 in federal foster care benefits on behalf of two clients, and another two clients who had been deemed ineligible kept receiving payments because of a child-welfare system conversion problem. A separate foster care finding showed the same pattern of weak controls after placement. Auditors tested 60 cases and found 36 children did not receive the required level-of-care assessment within 90 days, with delays ranging from 11 to 302 days. They also found one child's level-of-care designation was automatically changed by the child welfare information system under draft policies that had not been formally approved, generating $3,003 in questioned costs. Taken together, the audit describes a state government that kept moving money while basic oversight, procurement and child-safety controls lagged behind. Taken together, the audit describes a state government that kept moving money while basic oversight, procurement, and child-safety controls lagged behind. The audit also captured a blunt management response from DHHS. In the procurement finding, the department said "there is not a requirement to provide documentation" that personnel assertions on procurement justification forms are accurate. In other words, DHHS argued there's no requirement for them to tell the truth when they're directing taxpayer-funded contracts via no-bid contracts. Auditors rejected that argument, writing that without documentation supporting those assertions, "the best value for the State cannot be ensured." The same statewide procurement finding says the comprehensive purchasing policy and operations manual had not been formally updated since 2015. Accounting Errors and Procurement Risks The report detailed significant accounting lapses within the newly established Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) Fund -- the Democrat plan to levy a one-percent tax on paychecks so that workers can get paid vacations for pretty much any reason. Auditors found that accounts receivable were initially understated by $47 million, while $7.1 million in software expenditures were erroneously expensed rather than capitalized. That's an inauspicious beginning for a program that hasn't even started providing the alleged benefits to Maine's workers. Further fiscal friction was noted in individual income tax reporting. A methodology error resulted in a $119.3 million overstatement of taxes receivable and deferred inflows, requiring a retroactive restatement of the state's beginning net position. Big Picture: Nothing has changed since last years single annual report exposed more than $2.1 billion in spending at risk for fraud and corruption due to terrible internal controls. The last state audit, , said taxpayers were exposed to major financial risk because the state lacked basic oversight over contract spending and procurement controls. The audit found $2.1 billion in FY2024 contract payments were made under a system the audit found lacked adequate supervisory controls. Last year's report reviewed 45 procurement actions and found no documentation of cost analysis in any of them. They also found that 16 of 31 sole-source contracts lacked documentation of the required "reasonable investigation." In one case, a sole-source contract was approved only after the work had already been completed. In the audit published last year, auditors also found evidence that low-cost contracts were being used to avoid competitive bidding, a practice known as "stacking" contracts. In one example, a department awarded seven concurrent low-cost service contracts to the same vendor in a single year, which the article describes as a way to dodge oversight. The Mills Administration never commented publicly on the 2024 annual report and there's no evidence that any state employee was disciplined for the financial mismanagement. ? * You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. name: Chaz Molder
subject: A room full of teachers
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Molder for Congress
body:
I wouldn’t be here without them.

| | | | |
---
Hey Peter, a few weeks back, I spent some time with a group of retired teachers here in Maury County. Sitting with them and listening to their stories reminded me of how much they shaped my life. I’m a product of Maury County schools, where I had many mentors who pushed me to be serious about my school work and who believed in me before I ever considered running for office. In a place like this, people take the time to invest in each other. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/1A7wjsFMW78y73LTvAMpAg~~/AAUS1hA~/rPQfUwxX09ZKPUcu_ZeAazSr8FSMxwJQ4rEUvDWDCu0o-5QtuDnLQ1M_1k1dERMKnQA8a168FS8UbIA6TqyToBUgTwXAae-mlVRMgOoCTXbT5zcMNjjo9l1Az1llY5ePk9JrvN6XDd03PmHy-BMxg9Iiy3ducVxj_7d3xODlLGhLBVHOZMt9hGAmQdb0w4OGowLa_9A6pbEDH5CZn8Arl2cVv0KzHqH6Q2-sP146B3YL6jTDgvehHno6oHHDqIJg) That’s something I carry with me every day as mayor, and it’s a big part of why I’m running for Congress. Because the opportunities we had growing up in Columbia should still be within reach for the next generation — strong schools, good healthcare, and safe communities. That kind of foundation doesn’t happen by accident. It takes steady leadership and people willing to put in the work. As we head toward the end of this fundraising quarter, I’ve been thinking a lot about that and about what it takes to build something that lasts. **[If you’re able, will you chip in $10 to help us keep building a campaign rooted right here in Middle Tennessee?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/p-l4mqNQbMhWqyGZnW233Q~~/AAUS1hA~/OluXv5RwVMluE1DjVwnxhNezc5GZBPEVEqfM_Vucf0QsAer-cxALIS_Crkv2d3a00rmRvGA1gqRZNNzUiIuFRz67xlsgYh5-NiDDPwA1ty4dAbjBDa_BhAQ923LoY1cB6IlYszVjy64Fk3W5LqYYzQ5KYWjAVBdZpG4DPepP12dkhZS73B-Epv996SSyBFvXrX_VlpEF-WUVsDWd1jIxZMqQF6iDdiA1Cfw54FDnAFju7Lx25KwNNqYV0suQBa16SbXBUn_3pl5MorO6ETrteA~~)** | | [ CHIP IN $10](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/uTu1sKrjNEyXYJ7p1kU-6w~~/AAUS1hA~/OluXv5RwVMluE1DjVwnxhNezc5GZBPEVEqfM_Vucf0QsAer-cxALIS_Crkv2d3a00rmRvGA1gqRZNNzUiIuFRz67xlsgYh5-NiDDPwA1ty4dAbjBDa_BhAQ923LoY1cB6IlYszVjy64Fk3W5LqYYzQ5KYWjAVBdZpG4DPepP12cnf7MnRksxnxlLGi6QOywn5uG7nUETATXzU7NfZAmx0pGzqE-60PbWEJMm5aJ2sGaRL02f6Wg0BX3Wbr8jRpgPy4Cr7vdyqW3GxwTutG2BHA~~)

An ICE agent **[saved the life of a 1-year-old boy who stopped breathing](https://substack.com/redirect/1514545b-c17e-49b3-8361-91aa82bd3861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while in a TSA PreCheck line at New York City's JFK Airport on Wednesday, rushing to the scene after hearing the father's screams and performing the Heimlich maneuver.
Security footage showed the child's arms becoming lifeless in his father's arms, sparking panic as passengers scrambled to find help, before the agent assessed the child and began the lifesaving procedure.
## [Watch the heart-stopping moment here:](https://substack.com/redirect/1514545b-c17e-49b3-8361-91aa82bd3861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1514545b-c17e-49b3-8361-91aa82bd3861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/1514545b-c17e-49b3-8361-91aa82bd3861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **What happened:** After a few seconds, the child started breathing again, with responding paramedics evaluating the boy and determining he was healthy enough to fly. DHS said "this heroic officer immediately sprang into action--rushing toward the cries, taking the child, and performing a Heimlich maneuver that restored the infant's breathing after nearly two minutes," adding the officer's "extraordinary bravery embodies the selfless service of DHS law enforcement."
* **The pattern:** The boy was the second child saved by ICE in recent weeks--on Feb. 20, off-duty ICE agents in Plymouth, Massachusetts, performed CPR on a 4-year-old who fell into a hotel swimming pool and almost drowned after a panicked woman sought their help. ICE said at the time "if our agents had not been there and stepped up, this would have been a tragic outcome. Because of their training, these two agents were able to save a life."

When consumers give up, the markets fall quickly. 401(k)'s are in for a rough ride.
**Economists point to the "Expectations Index" as a key signal of America's financial health. When the Index is below 80, it's a major warning sign that a recession is near. In January, it fell to 65.**
This isn't just a dip, it's a declaration. Our economy relies on a strong job market and confident consumers buying goods. In 2026, America's working class is cutting non-essential spending.
The HR Executive reports "a worried and distracted workforce, whose concerns have them in "survival mode."
**This "crisis of confidence" may impact those near retirement the most. It indicates deep, structural stress in the framework holding up your 401(k)'s and IRA's.**
Most 401(k)s and IRAs are designed for "fair weather." They thrive when the economy is booming. They are not built to withstand the pressure of "a 12-year low in consumer confidence."

# **Chicago alderwoman closes office over backlash after saying slain student was in "wrong place at the wrong time"**
Chicago Alderwoman Maria Hadden **[closed her office for the week](https://substack.com/redirect/e23d77ac-2bec-4169-9ca4-d5607ff3bc90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** citing safety concerns after backlash over comments that Loyola University freshman Sheridan Gorman, 18, killed March 19 on a Rogers Park pier, was in the "wrong place at the wrong time" and might have "startled" her alleged killer.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/720cb938-870b-4363-b2ab-d6090fc68911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/720cb938-870b-4363-b2ab-d6090fc68911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The apology:** Hadden apologized Wednesday, saying her comments "landed wrong with some people" and were "never intended to blame the victim," adding "the fact that some media outlets are intentionally creating sound bites to misconstrue my words during this tragedy is also unfortunate."
* **Why it matters:** The suspect, Jose Medina-Medina, 25, is an illegal immigrant from Venezuela who was apprehended by Border Patrol in May 2023 then released into the U.S. under the Biden administration, according to DHS. He was charged with shoplifting in 2023 after allegedly stealing over $130 from a Macy's, failed to appear for court resulting in an active warrant when he allegedly shot Gorman, and is currently hospitalized with tuberculosis with his court hearing rescheduled for Friday.
* **What happened:** Police sources said the shooting was an apparent ambush with the suspect wearing a face mask, though he was later identified via video footage showing his "very distinct limp and gait" in his apartment building lobby. Court documents show Medina-Medina told officials in 2023 he was living at Leone Beach Park fieldhouse, a city-sponsored migrant shelter that closed in 2024.

# Chinese siblings charged in IED plot at US Iran War command base
A **[Chinese brother and sister have been charged](https://substack.com/redirect/bdb8f81c-af33-4408-9de8-97b454a2a577?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after an explosive device was found outside a gate at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, the headquarters of US Central Command overseeing troops in the Iran war, with the brother fleeing to China while the sister faces accessory charges.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bdb8f81c-af33-4408-9de8-97b454a2a577?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Device Found March 16:** The IED was discovered outside a gate at MacDill Air Force Base on March 16, days after it was allegedly planted between March 10 and 12 near the visitors center at the nerve center for US operations in the Middle East.
* **Charges Against Siblings:** Alen Zheng, 20, faces charges of attempting to damage government property, unlawfully making a destructive device, and possessing an unregistered destructive device; his sister Ann Mary Zheng, 27, is charged with witness tampering and accessory after the fact.
* **FBI Director Statement:** FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the sister is in custody while the brother Alen Zheng fled to China, with both sharing an address in Land O' Lakes near the base.

# Europe now has up to 1,000 No-Go Zones according to mass migration report
A new report presented to the EU Parliament estimates Europe is home to 900-1,000 "no-go zones" and thousands more sensitive neighborhoods, driven by decades of mass migration policies and failures of multiculturalism, **[with 63% of Islamist terror attacks from 2010 to 2025 linked to such areas.](https://substack.com/redirect/268a6b78-5c3c-4add-bee2-4af115ce606f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/268a6b78-5c3c-4add-bee2-4af115ce606f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Foreign-Born Population Spike:** No-go zones studied have an average 40% foreign-born population, more than 100% higher than the EU average of 20% and urban average of 30%, correlating directly with the rise in these high-crime enclaves.
* **Metrics Define No-Go Areas:** Areas are scored on homicide, sexual violence, robbery rates, youth gangs, unemployment, school dropouts, antisemitism, homophobia, gender restrictions, and state withdrawal such as police refusing entry, with the highest scoring 10 as de facto autonomous zones.
* **High-Scoring Neighborhoods Named:** Franc-Moisin in Saint-Denis, France scored 10; La Castellane in Marseille, Molenbeek in Brussels, and Rosengard in Malmo, Sweden each scored 9.4, showing extreme examples of parallel societies.
* **Report Author and Statement:** Authored by Maxime Hemery-Aymar and presented by New Direction Foundation, the report warns these enclaves exploit vulnerabilities for jihadist recruitment, with Nicola Procaccini stating they threaten the values of freedom and equality defining European civilization.

# Ex-Police chief allegedly steals $30,000 from kids' Christmas Fund in Georgia
Georgia Bureau of Investigation agents arrested former Pearson police chief Woodrow "Peewee" Wilson Burkhalter and charged him with 56 counts of theft after he and his wife allegedly misappropriated $30,000 from the Atkinson County **[Christmas fund meant for underprivileged children](https://substack.com/redirect/92ce2f23-6aa7-4ede-b14f-e353fe4f917f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** between November 2019 and January 2026.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/92ce2f23-6aa7-4ede-b14f-e353fe4f917f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Fund Manager Accused of Theft:** Burkhalter, designated as one of the managers of the fund while serving as chief, allegedly used his access to misappropriate the money intended to provide Christmas gifts to underprivileged children in Atkinson County.
* **Wife Faces Accessory Charges:** Burkhalter's wife Angela was charged with one count of party to the crime of theft by taking and one count of party to the crime of theft by conversion in connection with the missing $30,000.
* **Investigation Triggered in January:** The Atkinson County Sheriff's Office requested the GBI open an investigation in January 2026 after allegations surfaced that Burkhalter had misappropriated money from the children's Christmas fund.
* **Mayor Calls It Heartbreaking:** Pearson Mayor Jason Joyner stated it is a sad day for Pearson and Atkinson County, noting the funds meant for children during Christmas did not reach them, while emphasizing the current city leadership was not involved.

I’m calling on the Senate to do the right thing.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128133194/610348713/-153530995?refcode=EM_F_260325ACA_N_SB_90DO_4_NG_N_LOGO&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmIwMWExZi01ZjI5LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=OaxbLbTF6ujZ5MnnmO7k8SyvY_rrlCxAHCfH0YXWwe0=) Peter,

This week marked the anniversary of the Affordable Care Act. In honor of this historic legislation, **I have called on Senate Republicans to end their efforts to BLOCK the ACA's Enhanced Premium Tax Credits, which lowered healthcare costs.**

Because of Trump’s Big Ugly Law and the GOP’s indifference to the struggles of hardworking people, over 20 million Americans will lose healthcare coverage. This includes more than 500,000 Ohioans who have seen their healthcare costs skyrocket in the past year and forced to choose between paying rent or their mortgage and accessing care.

ICE continues to terrorize and brutalize our communities, Trump and Netanyahu are carrying out an illegal and unjustifiable war in Iran, the cost of living just keeps going up and up, and here at home, Ilhan just had a new challenger jump in the race for her seat.

| | | | | | Dear Peter,**If you want to understand what Congress really values, watch what they fund.** Right now, billions of dollars in military aid to Israel move through Washington with barely any resistance. There is no serious debate about cost, no real conditions, and no meaningful accountability. Funding for Israel is treated as automatic.
That urgency disappears when the conversation turns to healthcare, education, or housing here at home. Lawmakers slow down. They warn about costs and tell working families that real investment is out of reach.
**That contrast is not complicated. It is a choice.**
Congress always finds money to fund Israel’s war, even as it claims there is none to help people here afford a doctor, a home, or a decent education. These priorities reflect who our government is listening to and who it is not.
This is not about denying anyone’s right to safety. It is about whether our policies are actually creating it. What we are seeing is a system that treats military funding for Israel as urgent and human needs here as optional.
**That is not leadership. It is a failure of priorities.**
The candidates who take money from defense contractors and wartime industries are the same ones approving these blank checks. That money shows up later in their votes. Brad Sherman, our sitting Congressman, has been doing his part for almost thirty years to support Israel and its endless warmongering.
**This campaign is different.** We are funded by people who are tired of being told there is no money for their lives while billions are approved without question for Israel’s war.
If you want to change what Congress funds, you have to change who funds Congress.
[**Chip in today and help us fight for healthcare, education, and housing with the same urgency Washington gives to funding Israel’s war.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=9cebfaf313&e=53c7d12fc7)

As promised, here are the results from the Robinson Report pre- & post-debate surveys.
To state the obvious: This is not a random sample -- it's only subscribers to this Substack. Basic math means you need a sample size that's representative of the people who will turnout on primary election day for it to have some predictive value. Robinson Report subscribers, being smarter and prettier than your average Mainer, are not perfectly representative of the electorate. So you can't quite extrapolate the findings to the entire Republican Party, but the results -- and the changes between the two polls -- are interesting nonetheless. And it's the best data I have until these candidates start leaking me internal polls (hint, hint).

name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: A bright hot day at Texas State in San Marcos yesterday
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240767%2E444211%2ExVznWW)
A bright hot day at Texas State in San Marcos yesterday. No where I’d rather be:

We weren’t able to post up at the quad so didn’t get to see as many people, but grateful for everyone we met, registered and are staying in touch with going forward.
Alyssa, a freshman from Beaumont got her registration updated with us. Told me about challenges back home that she’d like to improve — education, lack of opportunity — and hopes that being more politically involved can make it better. Also, gas. Costs her $41 for half a tank. That same amount used to cover a full tank. She’s ready for change!
Met Jared from Dallas who is pursuing healthcare to be a family physician. His dream is to set up in underserved communities and bring a team of healthcare providers to give holistic care to anyone who needs it.
Destiny and Angel, first year roommates from Fort Worth, got registered together.
Saw student body president Abby Myers, in charge!
Met a guy who told me he just feels like giving up. He clarified that he’s not going to hurt himself, he means he just wants to give up on all of this. He told me it seems like the people in power just keep getting worse, more corrupt, more cruel and more powerful. What’s someone like him going to be able to do about it?
I told him we’re in this together, and it’s not him it’s all of us doing this together. I told him about Powered by People and our work registering and staying in touch with this new generation of voters. If we keep it up over the next 7 months, don’t give in to despair, keep this hope alive by doing the work, we’re going to make it. I invited him to join us and help with our work on campus and he said he would.
Talked to a woman from Venezuela who is a legal permanent resident but too afraid to leave the area because of an ICE presence in Buda. Doesn’t want to have to live in fear.
Diego told me he was getting registered because he knew it would make his grandmother happy (it will).
Lesa took care of everyone, even brought Easter eggs which she gave away at the end of her shift.
Best in show at Texas State Galleries Gabriela from El Paso!

Gallant and Dani go the distance.

Eat em up cats!
More soon,
Beto

name: Chris Brooks, LCV
subject: URGENT: Trump targets 45 million acres of forests — plan would allow clear-cutting for protected old-growth trees
body:
Through March 31, your gift TRIPLES for our forests.

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM1ODg0NDYS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQyMTE0MTYxMwS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
|
* * *
---
| | | | UPDATE... the Trump administration is moving forward with a sweeping plan to overturn the Roadless Rule and rollback protections for **45 million acres of land from logging and road construction, including old-growth forests** like the Tongass National Forest in Alaska.
---
| | **We need to start mobilizing our response NOW, Peter — and we need your help.** Because this moment is so important, a donor will 3X MATCH all contributions up to our $25,000 goal.
---
| | [**_Will you renew your LCV membership today to protect national forests from being turned into industrial work zones? $15 is all it takes >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | This attack on national forests would open the door to road-building, logging, and industrial development, jeopardizing our nation’s most treasured landscapes, threatening wildlife, clean drinking water, and old-growth forests that will take generations to replace.
---
| | It’s up to us to stand up against this move by the Trump administration, which could permanently alter _millions of acres of public lands and forests_. The public overwhelmingly supports the Roadless Rule and the administration needs to hear it — that means driving thousands of public comments from every corner of the country.
---
| | We’re going to need to make a lot of noise to force them to hear us, Peter. Timber companies have MAGA Republicans in their pockets and they have vast resources and connections — but this is a fight _we can win_ , if we have all of our members behind us.
---
| | [**_Please, renew for $15 before March 31 to TRIPLE your impact, every $1=$3 >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/RZbkcR-)
---
| | | [ TRIPLE YOUR IMPACT: RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >> ](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/j9y2f0D-)
---
| | Thank you for standing with us in this critical moment.
---
| | | | Chris Brooks
Vice President, Membership
League of Conservation Voters

Peter Willis,

Trump is lashing out, escalating his attacks on our movement – just as
headlines send him a clear message that No Kings Day this Saturday could
SHATTER records.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36228?source=email-20260326b&t=1062&akid=10449%2E5885482%2ESaGqUN ]Headline: 'Go Big and Go Lous': Inside the Justice Dept's push to
prosecute protesters

Trump and his allies are trying to intimidate, silence, and criminalize us
– instructing the Justice Department to “go big” in coming after
protesters. It’s a full-on coordinated attempt to chill dissent right
before No Kings Day, but we are NOT going to let it work.

Day too big, too bold, and too LOUD for Trump to ignore?

donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

Last year, Trump signed a new National Security directive (NSPM-7) that
singles out left-wing activists and launches a national strategy to
“investigate and disrupt” organizations like ours. And now news just
leaked that a top DOJ official told his staff they should be “hounding”
federal agents to bring cases using NSPM-7, demanding they “Go big, and go
loud.”

We have news for Trump: it isn’t going to work. We refuse to be silenced.
And with 3,000+ events planned across all 50 states, No Kings this
Saturday is going to be MASSIVE — if we can pull it off.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36228?source=email-20260326b&t=1061&akid=10449%2E5885482%2ESaGqUN ]Headline: No Kings March 28 protest expected to be largest in American
history: 3,000 events planned in all 50 states

Trump wants us to cower. But we are going bigger. We’re bringing the
noise. We’re pulling together toolkits for local organizers, printing
banners, and ensuring security is in place so that every event is strong,
safe, and impossible to ignore.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36228?t=1055&amount=22&refcode=email-20260326bnd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10449%2E5885482%2ESaGqUN ]If there was ever a time to show up with everything we’ve got, it’s now.
Will you donate to help us make March 28th the biggest day of protest in
history, and show Trump that his attempts to silence dissent will only
made us louder?

When we organize, we win.

Our Revolution

Peter, we’re five
days away from our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline — which means we
have five days to reach our $100,000 goal. Thanks to supporters like you,
we’ve made strong progress, but we’re not there just yet:

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260326-movement.JAKKac&refcode=em20260326-2079&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2079%2E342411%2EYf9cC0 ]Thermometer showing 46% of our $100,000 goal.

close the gap and power our movement forward?

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida have never backed down from their
bold visions for our democracy. Not in the face of corporate power, not in
the face of Trump’s ever-growing extremism, and not in the face of the
relentless attacks against them.

Day after day, the Squad continues to show what it means to fight for
justice, dignity, and rights for all communities — but this fight can’t be
won on tenacity alone.

Our movement stands out. While the forces working to defeat us and our
progressive champions continue to ramp up, no amount of money can
replicate what we’ve built together: real people-powered momentum.

That’s where you come in,
Peter. With the deadline just
days away, we need to keep building our grassroots strength, so the Squad
has the resources needed to defend their seats and turn their bold visions
for our democracy into reality.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260326-movement.JAKKac&refcode=em20260326-2079&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1004&akid=2079%2E342411%2EYf9cC0 ]Every contribution makes a difference. Will you chip in
$3 today to help us reach our $100,000 goal ahead of
Tuesday’s end-of-quarter deadline, and keep this movement strong?

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260326-movement.JAKKac&refcode=em20260326-2079&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1023&akid=2079%2E342411%2EYf9cC0 ]Contribute ››

Thank you for being part of our fight,

The Squad Victory Fund

clean_body: - Michele Tafoya here! I never really considered running for office. Ever. I was too focused on raising my family, and being the best football sideline reporter I could be. But even in the last few weeks, Minnesota has become the embodiment of everything wrong with politics today. Tim Walz, his inner circle, and the corrupt political class are too busy: Wasting billions of our tax dollars on fraudulent daycares Failing to condemn the activists storming churches Raising prices on hardworking families Sabotaging anything the President wants to do Forcing men into women's spaces Pitting Americans against each other I can 't sit on the sidelines anymore. That's why I'm throwing my hat in the ring and announcing my candidacy for U.S. Senate! thought long and hard about the dynamics of this race before jumping in. Minnesota has long been considered simply out of reach for Republicans. The last time it voted for a GOP President was Nixon. The pundits and political experts say a Republican could never win here. But this year is going to be different for three key reasons: FIRST - I'm running against Tim Walz's right hand. All the rampant fraud that took place here happened under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as it did under his. We will remind voters about that fact every single day. SECOND - The President has increased his voter share each time he has run. He nearly flipped this state in the last election, and Kamala Harris' running mate was our sitting Governor! Momentum is on our side. THIRD - I'm a different kind of candidate, and I know how to win. I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. And I kept fighting, no matter what the naysayers said. In my years on the sidelines, I 've seen a LOT of underdogs win football games that the "experts" said were impossible. The Minnesota Senate race will be another chapter in that storied history. | | ---|--- Thanks in advance for your support. I'll never forget the good folks who stepped up in the opening days of this campaign. You and I are going to do great things together. I can feel it. Be brave. Do good. - Michele Michele Tafoya Republican for Senate, Minnesota It's official - Michele Tafoya is running for U.S. Senate in Minnesota! Inside into the latest polling
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260326-2653)
Peter,
Leading the Marquette University Law School Poll three times in a row feels pretty good — we're not going to lie. But a poll number is just a snapshot. We wanted to understand _why_ we're winning and what it tells us about how we finish this race.
So we dug into the crosstabs. Here's what we learned:
1. **We're running on exactly what Wisconsin voters care about.**

Marquette asked voters what concerns them most: inflation (75% very concerned), health insurance (63%), jobs (60%), housing (57%), public schools (52%).
Now look at our platform: universal childcare. Paid family leave. Expanding BadgerCare. Fully funding public schools. A public bank for affordable capital. Taxing the ultra-wealthy to cut property taxes for regular folks.
2. **Independents are looking more blue than red — and winning them is key to winning this election.**

With just a few exceptions, independent voters are siding with Democrats on virtually every major issue in this poll. 73% disapprove of the attacks on Iran. 71% back the Supreme Court ruling against Trump on tariffs. 66% disapprove of the job Trump is doing.
Plus, Fran is the only Democratic candidate with a net positive favorability rating among independent voters.
3. **Union members are choosing the candidate who's lived the fight.**

Among union members who've made their choice in this primary — and nearly three-quarters already have — a majority (56%) are going with Fran. Her closest opponent is 21 points behind, and nobody else cracks double digits.
The people who organize for a living are choosing the bartender and line cook who built her career in kitchens. Not career politicians.
4. **Working-class Wisconsinites have turned on Trump.**

Among households making under $40,000 a year, Trump's disapproval is at 66%. Only 31% approve. 59% of all Wisconsin voters say his policies are making inflation worse — up 6 points in a single month. 60% say tariffs are hurting Wisconsin farmers. Only 16% say they're helping.
He promised to fight for working people. The people who fell for it are waking up.
5. **Fran built the cross-party coalition everyone else is still looking for.**

69% of Wisconsinites say data center costs outweigh the benefits — 62% of Republicans, 69% of independents, 77% of Democrats. Fran called for a moratorium in January, the first candidate in the race to do it.
61% disapprove of the attacks on Iran. Among independents, it's 73%. Fran opposed the strikes from day one.
**And here’s a bonus finding: 72% of Wisconsin still hasn't met Fran.**
This is where you come in. We’re asking you to help us make those introductions.
Reaching voters costs a truly insane amount of money. And in a seven-way primary where we're the only ones doing this without corporate cash, every dollar matters.
[Can you chip in $3, $10, or $27 today so we can get Fran in front of every voter in Wisconsin?](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260326.d0QzpA&refcode=em20260326-2653&t=1&akid=2653%2E105371%2EsrhT8o)

With gratitude,
Team Hong
